Lily and Sam nodded. They said, "We are sorry, Mom and Dad. We were greedy and we fought over the ring. We will not do that again. We will share and be careful."

Mom and Dad smiled. They said, "We are glad you learned your lesson. We love you, Lily and Sam. You are our precious fish."

Lily and Sam smiled too. They said, "We love you, Mom and Dad. You are the best." They hugged and kissed their mom and dad. Then they swam and played with their friends in the big reef. They were happy and safe.

"Excuse me, ma'am, I think I know where your ring is," he said.

"Really? Where?" the lady asked, hopeful.

"My sister has it. She found it yesterday and did not want to return it. But I will get it for you. Wait here, please," Tom said.

He ran to his sister and told her about the lady. He asked her to give back the ring.

"No, it is mine now. I like it too much. Go away!" Lily said, angry.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the ring on Lily's finger and the poster in Tom's hand. She understood what happened and scolded Lily.

Lily learned her lesson. She decided to be more generous and respectful. She and Tom became better friends and played happily in the park.

The moral of the story is: You should not take what is not yours and you should return what you find. Honesty and kindness are better than greed and selfishness.

To her surprise, the dog listened and walked away. Lily felt impressive and proud of herself for solving the conflict. From that day on, the cows were never scared again and Lily continued to play in the fields with her animal friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She was walking in the park on a sunny day with her mommy.

When they came to a spot on the grass, Sue noticed a large colourful butterfly. She was so impressed with its beauty that she quickly yelled out, "Wow mommy, look how impressive it is!" She wanted to get a closer look, so she got closer to the butterfly and tried to reach out to it. 

But as Sue got closer, the butterfly flew away. As it flew away, its wings sparkled in the sun and it seemed to freeze in the air.

Sue's mommy smiled and said, "Sometimes the best way to enjoy something beautiful is to just take a moment and admire it from a far. If you try too hard to get closer, you might scare it away." Sue nodded her head and looked around the spot to see if there were other impressive things she could admire, without trying to get too close. 

The moral of the story is that we should take time to appreciate the beauty all around us and not try to get too close - or we might miss the chance to see something special.

Once upon a time there was a bull who lived in a field. He had an original idea - he wanted to bathe in mud! So every day, he went to the same muddy spot to wallow.

The bull was so scared that he ran into the nearby forest. But the farmer was very angry, and because of that bad temper, the farmer set a fire to the forest. The fire spread quickly and soon, it was getting closer to the bull. 

The bull was so frightened that he charged blindly out of the forest, away from the fire. But the farmer did not stop - he continued to chase after the bull, determined to make him pay. Eventually, the bull collapsed from exhaustion and the bullying farmer stood triumphantly over him.

The bull had no choice but to accept his fate. He had suffered greatly, all because of his original idea to bathe in mud.

"I don't know," said a wise bear.

Once upon a time, there was a family that went to the mall. Dad was holding his daughter's hand while they walked around the mall. 
"Look at that toy store," said Dad with a smile. "Let's go and see what they have!"
But then, suddenly, the daughter felt something strange. She stopped and looked around.

The mall was totally dead. Everything was still, and no one was moving. 
"What happened, Dad?" asked the daughter.

Dad looked worried. "The mall had to yield to the virus," he said. "It's very sad, but everyone had to stay home."

The daughter's eyes widened. She had never heard of anything like this before. 
"What will we do now?" she asked. 

"Well," said Dad, "We can still explore the mall. We just have to be careful not to touch anything. And of course, no hugs or handshakes."

The daughter nodded, understanding. 
Together, they explored the mall, admiring the dead surroundings. 
They even enjoyed a snack, but with safety in mind. 

The daughter smiled. Even though the mall was dead, it still felt special to be there with Dad.

Once upon a time, there was a small lumberjack. He was very persistent and always tried hard at his job. But no matter how hard he tried, he just couldn't seem to cut down any trees. He was feeling sad when, suddenly, he heard a loud noise.

The lumberjack looked up and saw a mango tree shaking! The shaking stopped and then a voice said, "Please don't cut me down." The lumberjack was so surprised! He asked, "Who said that?" But there was no answer.

The lumberjack was very persistent, so he kept looking around and eventually he spotted a tiny creature. It was carrying a small saw and had a big hat on its head. The creature said, "I'm the tree fairy and I'm trying to protect the trees from being cut down!"

The lumberjack was so surprised he almost dropped his saw. Finally, he said, "OK, I won't cut down the trees if you promise to help me with my job." The tree fairy agreed and they began working together.

The tree fairy was such a big help that the lumberjack was soon able to cut down lots of trees. Every time he tried to cut down a tree, the tree fairy would stop him and suggest a better way.

The lumberjack was very happy with the help he was getting - but he also knew that he had to be persistent if he wanted to keep cutting down trees.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. Joe was three years old and he loved to play outside. One day, Joe wanted to play a game of tag with his friend Sally but when Joe asked Sally she said no. Joe felt sad and asked Sally why she wouldn't play. Sally replied, "I don't trust you. You told me a lie before." Joe was upset and confused, so Sally decided to explain. 

"Trust is when you are fair and tell the truth," Sally said. Joe thought about it and then asked, "Where can I find trust?" 

"It's like the grass in your backyard," Sally explained. "When it's sunny, the grass always stays the same. It's never different and never lies. That's what trust is like." Joe nodded and smiled, he'd found the answer he was looking for. 

From then on, Joe was always fair and he always told the truth. He remembered Sally's advice and made sure to trust others just like the grass in his backyard. 

The moral of the story is that trust is built by being fair and telling the truth. If you are trustworthy, others around you will also be trustworthy.

Lily liked her new bathtub. It was big and shiny and had a faucet that made bubbles. She wanted to play with her rubber duck and her boat in the water. She asked her mom if she could take a bath.

"Sure, honey, but don't make a mess," her mom said. "I'll be right back."

Lily ran to the bathroom and turned on the faucet. She filled the bathtub with warm water and bubbles. She put her rubber duck and her boat in the water and made them swim and splash. She was having so much fun.

But then she heard a strange noise. It sounded like a hiss and a pop. She looked around and saw a big hole in the wall. She saw a snake coming out of the hole. It had red eyes and sharp teeth. It looked at Lily and said, "Sssss, I'm hungry. I want to eat you and your toys."

Lily was scared. She screamed and jumped out of the bathtub. She ran to the door and tried to open it. But it was locked. She banged on the door and called for her mom.

"Mom, mom, help me! There's a snake in the bathroom!"

Her mom heard her and came running. She unlocked the door and opened it. She saw Lily crying and wet. She hugged her and asked her what happened.

"There's a snake in the bathtub, mom. It wanted to eat me and my toys."

Her mom looked at the bathtub. But she didn't see any snake. She only saw water and bubbles and a rubber duck and a boat. She didn't see any hole in the wall either.

"Where's the snake, Lily? I don't see any snake."

Lily pointed at the bathtub. But then she saw that the snake was gone. It had vanished. She didn't know where it went.

"It was there, mom. I saw it. It was big and scary. But now it's gone. It vanished."

Her mom didn't believe her. She thought Lily was making up stories. She told her to calm down and get dressed. She said she would drain the bathtub and clean the bathroom.

Lily didn't understand. She knew she saw the snake. She wondered if it would come back. She hoped it wouldn't. She didn't like her new bathtub anymore. She wanted her old one back.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. But sometimes they want the same toy. Then they fight.

One day, they see a new toy in the shop. It is a robot with a long arm. The arm can move and grab things. Anna and Ben both want the robot.

"Mom, can we have the robot?" they ask.

"Sorry, kids, we can only buy one robot. You have to share it," Mom says.

Anna and Ben are not happy. They both want the robot for themselves.

Mom buys the robot and gives it to Anna. She tells Ben to wait for his turn.

Anna takes the robot and plays with it. She makes the arm grab a ball, a book, and a hat. She laughs and says, "Look, Ben, the robot can do anything!"

Ben watches Anna. He is envious. He wants the robot too. He says, "Anna, give me the robot. It is my turn."

"No, it is not. I am still playing," Anna says.

"Yes, it is. Mom said we have to share," Ben says.

"No, it is not. Go away," Anna says.

They repeat the same words over and over. They start to yell and pull the robot.

Mom hears them and comes to see. She is not happy. She takes the robot and says, "Stop fighting, kids. You are not being nice. If you can't share the robot, you can't play with it at all."

She puts the robot on a high shelf. Anna and Ben can't reach it. They are sad and sorry.

They look at each other and say, "I'm sorry, Anna/Ben. I was mean. Can we be friends?"

They hug and say, "Yes, we can. We are twins. We love each other."

They go to play with their other toys. They share and have fun. They forget about the robot. Mom smiles and says, "That's better, kids. You are good twins."

"Wow, look at that ball!" Anna said. "I want to play with it!"

"Me too!" Ben said. "Let's get it!"

"Maybe we can use a chair," Anna said. She dragged a chair from the table and climbed on it. She was closer to the ball, but still not close enough.

"Maybe we can use a book," Ben said. He grabbed a book from the floor and gave it to Anna. She put it on the chair and stood on it. She was very close to the ball, but still not close enough.

"Maybe we can use a rope," Anna said. She saw a rope hanging from the ceiling. It was part of a lamp that their dad had made. She reached for the rope and pulled it. She hoped it would bring the ball closer to her.

But it did not. Instead, it made the lamp fall down. The lamp hit the shelf and knocked the ball off. The ball bounced on the floor and rolled away. The lamp broke into pieces and made a loud noise.

Anna and Ben were scared. They jumped off the chair and the book and ran away. They heard their mom coming from upstairs. She had heard the noise too.

"What happened here?" she asked. She saw the mess and the broken lamp. She was not happy.

"Sorry, mom," Anna and Ben said. "We just wanted to play with the amazing ball."

Tom and Anna were friends who liked to play with dolls. One day, they had a big fight. Tom wanted to play with Anna's new doll, but Anna said no. She said it was her doll and she did not want to share.

Tom was angry. He said, "You are mean and selfish. I hate you!" He grabbed Anna's new doll and ran away. Anna cried and chased him.

Tom ran to his room and locked the door. He looked at the new doll and felt bad. He did not really hate Anna. He was just jealous. He wanted to say sorry, but he did not know how.

He saw a pair of scissors on his desk. He had an idea. He thought, "Maybe if I cut the doll's hair, Anna will not like it anymore. Then she will not be mad at me. She will want to play with me again."

He took the scissors and started to cut the doll's hair. He cut and cut until the doll had no hair left. He looked at the doll and felt worse. He had ruined Anna's new doll. He had hurt her feelings. He was a bad friend.

He heard a knock on the door. It was Anna. She said, "Tom, please open the door. I want to talk to you. I am sorry I did not let you play with my new doll. I was wrong. I do not hate you. You are my friend."

Tom opened the door and saw Anna. She saw the doll and gasped. She said, "Tom, what did you do? You cut my new doll's hair! Why did you do that?"

Tom felt tears in his eyes. He said, "I am sorry, Anna. I did not mean to. I was angry and stupid. I wanted to make you not like the doll. I wanted you to play with me. I am sorry. I am sorry. I am sorry."

Anna looked at Tom and saw that he was sad. She felt sorry for him. She said, "Tom, it is okay. I forgive you. The doll's hair does not matter. You matter. You are my friend. I still like you. I still want to play with you."

Tom hugged Anna and said, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend. I am sorry I hurt you. I will never do that again. I love you."

Anna hugged Tom and said, "I love you too, Tom. Come on, let's go and play. Maybe we can find a hat for the doll."

They smiled and went to play. They forgot about the fight and the doll. They were happy again. The day was not gloomy anymore. It was bright and sunny.

Mia climbs the steps to the slide. She counts the steps. One, two, three, four, five. She is not at the top. She looks up. She is sad.

Tom slides down the slide. He goes fast. He laughs. He lands on the ground. He is proud.

Mia slides down the slide. She goes slow. She cries. She lands on the ground. She is scared.

Tom and Mia hug. They are friends. They seem happy. They go to play on the swings. They have fun.

Lily likes to draw with her crayons. She has many colors and she makes pictures of her family, her toys and her pets. She likes to show her drawings to her mom and dad and they say she is very good.

One day, Lily wants to draw a snowman. She remembers how she saw snow outside last winter and how she and her dad made a snowman in the yard. She thinks snow is very cold and white and soft. She takes a blue paper and starts to draw a big circle for the snowman's body. Then she draws a smaller circle for the head. She adds a carrot for the nose, two buttons for the eyes and a scarf for the neck.

She is almost done, but she needs to draw the arms and the hat. She looks for a brown crayon for the arms, but she cannot find it. She has used all her crayons and they are all over the table. She feels sad and says, "Oh no, I can't complete my snowman. I need a brown crayon for the arms and a hat."

Her mom hears her and comes to see what is wrong. She sees Lily's drawing and says, "Wow, Lily, your snowman is very nice. You are very creative. But why are you sad?"

Lily shows her mom the blue paper and says, "I can't complete my snowman. I need a brown crayon for the arms and a hat. But I don't have a brown crayon. I used all my crayons."

Her mom smiles and says, "Don't worry, Lily. I have a solution. You can use something else to make the arms and the hat. How about these?" She gives Lily two sticks and a woolen cap from her closet. "You can glue these on your paper and your snowman will be complete."

Lily's eyes light up and she says, "Thank you, mom. You are very smart. I will glue these on my paper and my snowman will be complete." She takes the sticks and the cap and glues them on her paper. She looks at her snowman and says, "Look, mom, my snowman is complete. He has arms and a hat. He is very cold and happy."

Her mom hugs her and says, "You are very welcome, Lily. Your snowman is complete and beautiful. You are very cold and happy too." They laugh and cuddle and look at the snowman on the blue paper.

Jen pointed to the juice and said, "I wanted juice, but I fell down. It hurts." Mom said, "I'm sorry, Jen. You should ask me for help. Don't climb on chairs. They are not safe. Here, I'll get you some juice. And some ice for your head."

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. But today, they saw something new. There was a big pole with a red and white stripe. It had a shiny ball on top.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Let's go and see."

They ran to the pole and touched it. It was cold and hard. They looked up at the ball. It was bright and round.

"Maybe it's a candy," Lily said. "Maybe we can eat it."

"No, it's not a candy," Ben said. "It's too high and too big. And it doesn't smell good."

They heard a loud noise. It was a siren. They saw a big truck with a ladder. It stopped near the pole. A man in a yellow hat and a black coat got out. He had a hose and a helmet.

"Hello, kids," he said. "Do you know what this is?"

They shook their heads.

"This is a fire hydrant," he said. "It helps us put out fires. We need to check it and make sure it works. Can you move away a little bit?"

They nodded and stepped back. They watched the man open a valve and spray water from the hose. The water made a rainbow in the sun.

"Wow," Lily said. "That's so cool."

The man smiled and closed the valve. He rolled up the hose and put it back in the truck.

"Thank you for being careful," he said. "You can play here again, but don't climb on the pole, okay? It's not a toy."

"Okay," Ben said. "Thank you for showing us."

The man waved and drove away. Lily and Ben looked at the pole again.

"It's not a candy," Lily said.

"It's not a toy," Ben said.

"But it's still pretty," Lily said.

They ran to the slide and played some more. They were restless and curious. They liked to learn new things.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with yellow fruits. "Look, lemons!" Lily said. "I like lemons. They are sour and juicy."

"Me too," Ben said. "Let's pick some and make lemonade." They ran to the tree and reached for the lemons. But the tree was too high for them. They could not get any lemons.

They saw a man with a ladder. He was picking lemons from the tree. He had a big basket full of lemons. "Excuse me, sir," Lily said. "Can we have some lemons, please? We want to make lemonade."

The man looked at them and smiled. "Sure, you can have some lemons," he said. "You are very polite. Here, take as many as you want." He gave them some lemons from his basket. He was very generous.

"Thank you, sir," Ben said. "You are very kind. Can we do something for you?"

The man thought for a moment. "Well, there is one thing you can do for me," he said. "You can save some lemonade for me. I would love to taste your lemonade. It must be very good."

Lily and Ben nodded. "Of course, we will save some lemonade for you," they said. "We will come back when we are done." They ran to their home with the lemons. They squeezed the lemons and added water and sugar. They made a big pitcher of lemonade. They poured some lemonade into a cup and covered it with a napkin. They wrote a note for the man: "This is for you. Thank you for the lemons. Lily and Ben."

They took the cup and the note and went back to the park. They found the man and gave him the cup and the note. The man was very happy. He drank the lemonade and said, "This is the best lemonade I ever had. You are very good at making lemonade. And you are very generous. Thank you for saving some lemonade for me. Lily and Ben."

Lily and Ben smiled. They learned that it is nice to share and to be grateful. They made a new friend. They enjoyed the rest of the lemonade together. They had a fun day.

"Come here, bunny!" Anna said. She ran to the rabbit and tried to catch it. But the rabbit was fast and ran away.

"Oops!" Ben said. He looked at the sock and laughed.

"That's not a bunny, silly!" Anna said. She laughed too.

"Hey, kids, have you seen my rabbit?" the man asked. "He's white and fluffy and has a red bow."

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for the man.

"Sorry, mister, we don't know where your rabbit is," Anna said.

"But we found your sock," Ben said. He gave the sock to the man.

The man smiled and thanked them. He looked at the sock and said, "This is not my sock. This is my rabbit's sock. He likes to wear it sometimes. He must have left it in the hole."

Anna and Ben were surprised. They looked at the hole and saw a white rabbit peeking out. He had a red bow on his neck.

"There he is!" the man said. He went to the hole and picked up the rabbit. He hugged him and said, "I'm so glad I found you, Fluffy. You're such a naughty rabbit."

"Mom, what is wrong with that fish?" Ben asked, pointing at the big fish.

Mom looked at the fish and frowned. She did not want to scare Ben and Lily.

"That fish is dead, Ben. It means it is not alive anymore. It does not swim or eat or breathe," mom said, gently.

Ben and Lily did not understand. They had never seen a dead thing before.

"Why is it dead, mom?" Lily asked, looking sad.

Mom did not know how to explain. She hugged Ben and Lily and said, "Sometimes, things die, honey. It is part of life. But we can remember them and be thankful for them. Do you want to say goodbye to the fish?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They took off their sunglasses and threw them into the pond. They said, "Goodbye, fish. Thank you for being shiny. We hope you are happy now."

Mom smiled and kissed Ben and Lily. She said, "You are very kind, my loves. Come on, let's go and play on the swings."

Ben and Lily ran to the swings, feeling a little sad, but also happy. They liked the park and the ducks and the fish. They liked their mom and their sunglasses. They liked life.

"Let me turn the jug," Sara said. She wanted to pour some juice in her cup.

"No, let me turn the jug," Ben said. He wanted to pour some juice in his cup.

They both pulled the jug and it started to wobble. The juice spilled on the table and on the floor. Sara and Ben gasped.

"Oh no, we made a mess!" Sara said.

"Mama will be angry!" Ben said.

They heard Mama coming. They quickly jumped off the chairs and ran to hide behind the sofa. They hoped Mama would not see them or the jug.

Mama entered the kitchen and saw the juice everywhere. She frowned and shook her head.

"Who turned the jug and made this mess?" she asked.

Sara and Ben peeked from behind the sofa. They felt sorry and scared. They came out and said in a small voice:

"We did, Mama. We were eager to drink some juice. We are sorry."

Mama sighed and smiled. She hugged Sara and Ben and said:

"It's okay, my loves. I know you were thirsty. But next time, please ask me before you turn the jug. And be careful not to spill the juice. Now, let's clean up together and then you can have some juice."

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and trains. They have a big network of tracks and roads on the floor. They can make the cars and trains go fast or slow.

One day, Tom has a new car. It is blue and shiny. It has a button that makes it go very fast. Tom wants to test his new car on the network. He says to Sam, "Look at my new car! It is the best car ever! It can go faster than any car or train!"

Sam is happy for Tom, but he also likes his old car. It is red and has stickers on it. It does not have a button, but it can still go fast. Sam says to Tom, "Your car is nice, but my car is nice too. It can go fast enough for me. Can we play together?"

Tom says, "No, I want to test my new car. It is better than your car. It can go faster than your car. Watch me!" He pushes the button and makes his car zoom on the network. He does not look where he is going. He does not care about Sam.

Sam is sad and angry. He does not like how Tom is acting. He thinks Tom is being mean and selfish. He says to Tom, "Stop! You are not being a good friend! You are not sharing the network! You are making a mess! You are crashing into my car and my train!"

Tom does not listen to Sam. He keeps pushing the button and making his car zoom. He thinks he is having fun. He does not see that he is hurting Sam's feelings. He does not see that he is breaking the network. He does not see that his car is getting scratched and dirty.

Then, something bad happens. Tom's car goes too fast and hits a wall. It makes a loud noise and breaks into pieces. Tom is shocked and scared. He cries and says, "Oh no! My new car! It is broken! It is ruined!"

Sam hears Tom cry and runs to him. He sees the broken car and the broken network. He feels sorry for Tom, but he also feels angry. He says to Tom, "I told you to stop! I told you to be careful! I told you to be a good friend! But you did not listen! You only cared about your new car! Now look what you did!"

Tom looks at Sam and feels ashamed. He knows he was wrong. He knows he was not a good friend. He says to Sam, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry I was mean and selfish. I'm sorry I did not share the network. I'm sorry I broke your car and your train. I'm sorry I broke my car and the network. Can you forgive me?"

Sam looks at Tom and sees that he is sincere. He sees that he is sad and sorry. He says to Tom, "I forgive you, Tom. I'm sorry I was angry. I know you liked your new car. I know you wanted to test it. But you have to be careful and respectful. You have to think about others. You have to be a good friend."

Tom nods and hugs Sam. He says, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend. You are a better friend than my new car. Can we fix the network and play together?"

Sam smiles and nods. He says, "Yes, Tom. We can fix the network and play together. We can use both our cars and our trains. We can have fun and be safe. We can be good friends."

The moral of the story is: Don't be mean and selfish. Share and care. Be a good friend.

Ben and Lily were twins who loved to look at the sky. Every night, they would go to their window and try to find the moon and the stars. Sometimes the moon was big and round, and sometimes it was small and thin. Sometimes it was bright and white, and sometimes it was yellow or orange.

One night, Ben and Lily saw something very special in the sky. It was a little moon, but it had a ring of light around it. It looked like a shiny donut. Ben and Lily were very excited. They ran to their mom and dad and said, "Look, look, there is a little moon with a ring!"

Mom and Dad smiled and hugged them. They said, "That is called a lunar eclipse. It happens when the earth comes between the sun and the moon, and makes a shadow on the moon. The ring of light is the sun shining through the edge of the earth. It is very rare and beautiful."

Ben and Lily wanted to know more. They asked, "Why does the earth come between the sun and the moon? How long does the lunar eclipse last? Can we touch the ring of light?"

Mom and Dad explained, "The earth, the sun and the moon move around in space. Sometimes they line up in a special way, and that is when we see a lunar eclipse. It only lasts for a few minutes, so we have to enjoy it while we can. And no, we cannot touch the ring of light. It is very far away, and very hot."

Ben and Lily nodded. They went back to their window and watched the little moon with the ring. They felt very lucky and happy. They said, "Thank you, earth, sun and moon, for making such a pretty picture for us. Good night, little moon. Good night, ring of light. We love you."

One day, they decided to be kings and queens. They put on their crowns and capes and sat on their chairs. They pretended to have a big feast and a party. They invited their toys and dolls to join them. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Tom saw something that made him jump. He saw a big spider on the curtain. He was scared of spiders. He screamed and ran away. Lily saw the spider too. She was not scared of spiders. She thought they were impressive. She reminded Tom that spiders were not bad. They were small and helpful. They made webs and ate bugs.

She took a paper cup and a paper plate and went to the curtain. She carefully put the cup over the spider and slid the plate under it. She lifted the cup and the plate and carried them to the window. She opened the window and let the spider go outside. She waved goodbye to the spider.

She went back to Tom and hugged him. She told him he was brave and kind. She asked him if he wanted to play pretend again. He nodded and smiled. They went back to their curtain and continued their game. They were happy.

Tom saw a butterfly in the garden. It was yellow and black and very pretty. He wanted to hold it in his hand. He ran after it and tried to catch it.

"Come here, butterfly!" he said. "I want to play with you!"

But the butterfly did not want to play with Tom. It flew away from him and hid behind a flower. Tom was angry. He stomped his feet and shouted.

"Stop flying away, butterfly! You are not nice!"

He reached out his hand and grabbed the butterfly by its wing. He felt it flutter in his palm. He smiled.

"I got you, butterfly! Now you are mine!"

But the butterfly did not like being held by Tom. It was hurt and scared. It wanted to be free. It tried to escape from Tom's hand. It made a tiny sound.

"Please, let me go, Tom!" it said. "You are hurting me! I want to fly in the sun!"

Tom heard the butterfly's voice. He was surprised. He looked at the butterfly in his hand. He saw its wing was broken. He felt sorry for the butterfly.

"I'm sorry, butterfly!" he said. "I did not mean to hurt you. I just wanted to be your friend."

He opened his hand and let the butterfly go. The butterfly flew away as fast as it could. It did not look back at Tom.

Tom watched the butterfly disappear. He felt sad and lonely. He wished he had been more gentle and kind. He learned a lesson that day.

He never tried to hold a butterfly again.

Lily starts to cry. She picks up the pieces of her drawings and hugs them. She wishes Max would be nice to her and not ruin her things.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees Lily crying and Max smirking. She sees the torn drawings on the floor. She knows what happened.

She scolds Max and tells him to apologize to Lily. She tells him to share and respect his sister's things. She tells him to make a new drawing for Lily and put it in her folder.

She hugs Lily and tells her that her drawings are beautiful and creative. She tells her that she loves her and her art. She helps her put the drawings back in her folder and zips it up.

Lily feels better and smiles. She thanks Mom and hugs her. She looks at her folder and feels happy. She still likes to draw with her crayons and keep her drawings in her folder. She hopes Max will be nicer to her and maybe draw with her someday.

"That's very nice, Lila. You are very creative," mom said, smiling.

"That's very cool, Sam. You are very clever," dad said, nodding.

Lila and Sam were happy and kept playing. They did not notice that the tide was coming in. The tide was the water that moved up and down the beach. Sometimes it was low and left more sand to play on. Sometimes it was high and covered some of the sand with water.

The sun was very hot that day. It made the sand and the water and the air hot too. It also made the ice cream truck come to the beach. The ice cream truck had a bell that rang and a sign that said "Ice Cream". It had many kinds of ice cream in cones and cups and sticks.

Lila and Sam heard the bell and saw the sign. They loved ice cream. They ran to their mom and dad and asked for some.

"Can we have ice cream, please?" they said together.

"Sure, you can have ice cream. But first, you have to clean up your sand toys and put them in the bag. And don't forget your hats and sunscreen. It's very hot today," mom said.

Lila and Sam agreed and ran back to their sand shapes. They were surprised to see that the tide had come in and washed away some of their sand shapes. The starfish and the boat were gone. Only some lumps of sand were left.

"Oh no, our sand shapes!" Lila said, sad.

"They melted!" Sam said, confused.

"No, they didn't melt. The tide took them away. The tide is the water that moves up and down the beach. Remember?" mom said, coming to them.

Lila and Sam nodded. They understood. They were still sad, but they also learned something new. They picked up their buckets and shovels and shells and sticks and put them in the bag. They put on their hats and sunscreen and followed their mom and dad to the ice cream truck.

They each got a cone of ice cream. Lila got vanilla and Sam got chocolate. They licked their ice cream and smiled. They still liked the beach and the sand and the tide. Lisa and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw.

One day, they see a big clock in the park. It has numbers and hands that move. Lisa and Tom are curious. They want to know what it is.

They go closer to the clock and look at it. They see a man standing next to the clock. He is wearing a hat and a coat. He has a watch on his wrist.

"Hello, children," the man says. "Do you like the clock?"

"Yes, we do," Lisa and Tom say. "It is very big and pretty. What is it for?"

The man smiles. "The clock tells the time. Time is how we measure how long things take. For example, how long you play in the park, or how long you sleep at night. The clock has numbers from one to twelve, and two hands that point to the numbers. The big hand is for minutes, and the small hand is for hours. Do you understand?"

Lisa and Tom nod. They think the clock is very clever. They admire the clock and the man.

"Can you tell me what time it is now?" the man asks.

Lisa and Tom look at the clock. They try to remember what the man said. They see that the big hand is pointing to the six, and the small hand is pointing to the three.

Lisa says, "It is six and three."

Tom says, "No, it is three and six."

They look at each other. They are not sure who is right.

The man laughs. "You are both a little bit right, and a little bit wrong. It is not six and three, or three and six. It is three thirty. That means it is half past three. You say half past when the big hand is pointing to the six. Do you see?"

Lisa and Tom see. They feel embarrassed. They did not know how to say the time. They say sorry to the man.

The man says, "Don't be sorry. You are very smart and brave to try. Learning the time is not easy. It takes practice. You will learn it soon. Do you want me to teach you more?"

Lisa and Tom say yes. They want to learn more. They like the clock and the man. They thank him for his help.

They stay with the man for a while. He teaches them how to say the time in different ways. He shows them his watch and how it works. He tells them stories about the clock and the park.

Lisa and Tom have a lot of fun. They learn a lot. They make a new friend. They are happy.

Lily liked to bounce on her bed. She bounced up and down, up and down, with a big smile on her face. She liked to pretend she was a kangaroo or a rabbit or a frog. She bounced so high that she could touch the ceiling.

One day, she bounced too hard and her bed broke. She heard a loud crack and felt the mattress sink. She was scared and sad. She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and said it was okay. She said they would get a new bed for her.

Lily asked her mom if she could still bounce on the new bed. Her mom said yes, but not too much. She said bouncing was fun, but it could also be dangerous. She said Lily should be careful and not bounce too close to the edge or the window or the lamp.

Lily said she understood. She said she was sorry for breaking her bed. Her mom said she forgave her. She said she loved her very much. She said she would read her a story to make her feel better.

Lily smiled and said she liked stories. She asked her mom to read her a story about bouncing. Her mom said she knew a good one. She picked up a heavy book from the shelf. It was a book of fairy tales. She opened it and found a story about a princess and a pea. She said it was a story about a very bouncy bed. Lily was curious and excited. She cuddled with her mom and listened to the story. She liked the story very much. She felt happy and sleepy. She fell asleep in her mom's arms.

Tim and Sam are best friends. They like to play with their toy trucks in the park. They make loud noises and pretend to drive on the road.

One day, they see a big truck parked near the park. It is yellow and shiny. It has a long trailer behind it. Tim and Sam are curious. They want to see the truck up close.

They run to the truck and climb on the trailer. They see many boxes inside. They wonder what is in the boxes. They open one box and find a big teddy bear. It is soft and chubby. Tim and Sam are happy. They hug the teddy bear and smile.

"Look, Sam, a teddy bear!" Tim says.

"Wow, Tim, it is so nice!" Sam says.

They hear a loud honk. They look up and see the truck driver. He is angry. He yells at them.

"Hey, you kids, get off my truck! This is not a toy! This is my job!" he says.

He jumps out of the truck and walks to the trailer. He grabs the teddy bear from Tim and Sam. He puts it back in the box. He closes the box and locks the trailer.

He tells Tim and Sam to go away. He says they are naughty and rude. He says they could get hurt or break something.

Tim and Sam are scared and sad. They run away from the truck. They cry and say sorry.

They go back to their toy trucks. They play quietly and carefully. They do not want to make the truck driver mad again.

They learn to respect other people's things. They also learn to reverse their toy trucks. They think reversing is fun and cool. They hope the truck driver will forgive them and maybe share his teddy bear with them someday.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their dad's equipment. They saw a big machine with buttons and levers and wires. They wanted to see what it did.

"Let's try this one," Tim said, and pulled a lever. The machine made a loud noise and a light flashed.

"Wow, cool!" Sam said, and pushed a button. The machine made another noise and a different light flashed.

They kept pulling and pushing and turning things on the machine. They did not know that the machine was very delicate and important. They did not know that the machine was measuring the water in the lake.

The more they played, the more the machine increased the water in the lake. The water rose higher and higher, until it reached the edge of the shore. Then it spilled over and flooded the land.

Soon, the water reached their house. Their dad saw the water and ran outside. He saw the machine and his sons.

"What have you done?" he shouted. "You have ruined the machine and the lake and the house! You are in big trouble!"

Tim and Sam were scared and sorry. They did not mean to cause so much damage. They wished they had not played with the machine. They wished they had listened to their dad. But it was too late. The water kept rising and they had nowhere to go.

The museum was very busy. There were many people looking at the things. Tom and Lily had to hold Mom and Dad's hands so they would not get lost. Sometimes they had to wait in line to see something. Sometimes they had to move away from something because it was too crowded.

Tom and Lily felt different things at the museum. They felt curious when they saw something new. They felt happy when they saw something they liked. They felt bored when they saw something they did not care about. They felt tired when they walked a lot. They felt hungry when it was time for lunch.

At the end of the day, Tom and Lily felt glad that they went to the museum. They learned a lot and had fun. They thanked Mom and Dad for taking them. They said they wanted to come back again. They felt sleepy when they got in the car. They closed their eyes and dreamed of the things they saw.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big puddle near the slide. Lily wanted to splash in the puddle, but Tom said no.

"Mom said we should not get wet and dirty," Tom said. "We should play on the slide or the swings."

But Lily did not listen. She ran to the puddle and jumped in. She made a big splash and laughed. She felt the water on her feet and legs. She thought it was fun.

Tom watched her and shook his head. He went to the slide and climbed up the steps. He slid down and felt the wind on his face. He thought it was fun too.

Then, Lily saw a duck near the puddle. She wanted to splash the duck and make it quack. She ran to the duck and kicked the water. But the duck did not like it. It flapped its wings and pecked Lily's foot. Lily cried out and ran away. She felt the pain on her foot and the mud on her clothes. She did not think it was fun anymore.

Tom heard her cry and ran to her. He saw the duck and the puddle and the mud. He felt sorry for Lily. He hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I will help you."

He took her to the bench and wiped her foot with a tissue. He gave her his sweet that he had in his pocket. He said, "Here, Lily. Have this. It will make you feel better."

Lily took the sweet and smiled. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I'm sorry I did not listen to you. I learned my lesson. I will not splash the duck again."

Tom smiled too. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good sister. I'm glad you are okay. I learned something too. I will not be too bossy. We can both have fun in different ways."

They hugged each other and went to play on the swings. They were happy and they forgot about the puddle and the duck. They learned to be kind and respectful to each other and to the animals.

One day, Jen and Ben are playing in their room. Jen wants to play with Ben's car, but Ben says no. He says it is his car and he likes it. Jen gets mad and says she will not give him her doll. Ben says he does not care. He says dolls are for girls and cars are for boys.

Jen has an idea. She goes to the closet and finds a strip of cloth. She wraps the cloth around the car and makes it look like a doll. She says to Ben, "Look, I have a new doll. It is purple and pretty. Do you want to play with it?" Ben says yes. He thinks it is a real doll. He gives Jen his car and takes the cloth doll.

Jen is happy. She has both the car and the doll. She plays with them and makes them go fast and talk. Ben is happy too. He likes the purple doll. He hugs it and makes it sing.

But then, the cloth falls off the car. Ben sees that it is not a doll, but his car. He is angry and sad. He says to Jen, "You tricked me! You gave me a fake doll and took my car. That is not nice. Give me back my car!" Jen says no. She says it is her car now and she likes it. They start to fight and yell.

Mom hears them and comes to the room. She sees the car, the doll, and the cloth. She knows what happened. She says to Jen and Ben, "Stop fighting, you two. You need to share your toys and be kind to each other. Jen, you should not trick your brother and take his car. Ben, you should not be mean to your sister and refuse to play with her doll. Now, give each other a hug and say sorry. Then, you can play with both the toys together." Jen and Ben do what Mom says. They hug and say sorry. They play with the car and the doll together. They are happy again. Mom smiles and says, "That's better. I love you both."

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the hall. They have many toys: cars, dolls, balls, blocks. But they do not like to wash their toys. They leave them dirty and messy on the floor.

One day, Mom comes to the hall. She sees the toys and she is not happy. She says to Lily and Ben: "Look at your toys! They are so dirty and messy! You need to wash them and put them away. Or else, you will have no toys to play with."

Lily and Ben do not want to wash their toys. They say to Mom: "No, Mom, we do not want to wash our toys. We want to play with them. Washing is boring and hard. Please, Mom, let us play."

Mom shakes her head. She says to Lily and Ben: "No, Lily and Ben, you have to wash your toys. It is not fair to leave them dirty and messy. They are your friends. You have to take care of them. Think of the poor toys. How do you think they feel?"

Lily and Ben look at their toys. They see the dirt and the dust on them. They think of the poor toys. They feel sorry for them. They say to Mom: "OK, Mom, we will wash our toys. We are sorry. We love our toys. We want them to be clean and happy."

Mom smiles. She says to Lily and Ben: "That's good, Lily and Ben. I am proud of you. You are good children. Now, let's wash your toys together. It will be fun and easy. And then, you can play with them again."

Lily and Ben nod. They take their toys to the sink. They wash them with soap and water. They dry them with a towel. They put them away in their boxes. "Meet Coco," Mom said. "She is your new puppy. We are proud of you for behaving and being responsible. We think you are ready to have a pet."

You have to feed them, water them, and give them a place to sleep. You have to train them, play with them, and keep them safe. Do you understand?"

"Yes, we understand," Lily and Ben said. They nodded and smiled. They were ready to be good puppy owners.

"Okay, then. Have fun with Coco. But be careful. There are cars and other animals outside. Stay close to us and don't let go of the leash. We want you and Coco to be safe," Mom said.

Lily and Ben agreed. They followed Mom and Dad outside with Coco. They walked around the block and saw other people and dogs. Coco was curious and friendly. She sniffed and licked and barked. Lily and Ben laughed and petted her. They loved their new puppy. They were happy and safe.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play with puzzles. They have many puzzles with animals, cars, and flowers. Sara and Ben can solve puzzles very fast. They are good at finding the right pieces.

One day, Sara and Ben find a new puzzle. It is a puzzle of a lime. A lime is a green fruit that is sour. Sara and Ben have never seen a lime before. They are curious. They want to solve the lime puzzle.

They open the box and dump the pieces on the floor. They start to look for the edges. But they have a problem. All the pieces are green. They are the same color as the lime. Sara and Ben cannot tell them apart. They are confused. They do not know how to solve the lime puzzle.

They try to match the shapes, but they do not fit. They try to look at the picture on the box, but they do not see any clues. They try to ask their mom, but she is busy. Sara and Ben are frustrated. They are not having fun.

They are about to give up, when they hear a voice. It is their friend Leo. Leo is older than Sara and Ben. He knows many things. He sees the lime puzzle and says, "Hi, Sara and Ben. Do you need help?"

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, please. We cannot solve the lime puzzle. It is too hard. All the pieces are green."

Leo smiles. He says, "I can help you. I have solved the lime puzzle before. It is not too hard. You just need to look for the details. The lime has a stem, a skin, and a pulp. The stem is darker than the skin. The skin has bumps and spots. The pulp has wedges and seeds. If you look closely, you can see the differences. Here, let me show you."

Leo sits down with Sara and Ben. He picks up a piece and points to the stem. He says, "This is the stem. It is where the lime grows on the tree. It is darker than the rest of the lime. Can you find another piece with the stem?"

Sara and Ben look at the pieces. They find another piece with the stem. They put them together. They see that they fit. They are happy. They say, "Thank you, Leo. You are smart. You know how to solve the lime puzzle."

Leo says, "You are welcome, Sara and Ben. You are smart, too. You just need to pay attention. Sometimes, things that look the same are different. You need to look for the details. That is how you solve puzzles. And not just puzzles, but also problems. Do you want to solve the lime puzzle with me?"

Sara and Ben say, "Yes, we do. We want to learn from you. We want to solve puzzles and problems. We are ready."

They work together with Leo. They look for the details. They find the pieces with the skin, the pulp, and the seeds. They match them and make the lime. They are proud. They have solved the lime puzzle.

The moral of the story is: Look for the details. They can help you solve puzzles and problems.

Inside the castle Sarah saw a huge room with a beautiful throne. The Princess asked Sarah to take off her veil and she did it. The Princess sat in the throne and asked Sarah to sit beside her. Both of them smiled. They were so happy to meet each other.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Henrik. He was only three years old and he loved to poke. Every day he would go outside and poke around in the dirt, rocks and leaves. 

One day he saw an old man. The old man told Henrik a story. It was a kind story about a prince and princess. Henrik listened closely and thought it was the best story ever. He asked the old man to tell him the story again. 

Henrik liked the story so much that he wanted to share it with his friends. So he went to the park and found his friends. Henrik carefully poked each of his friends in turn so that they would gather around and listen to the story. His friends liked the story and they took turns poking each other so that they could listen to the story again and again. 

From then on, Henrik and his friends loved to play and poke around. But most of all, they loved to listen to the kind story that the old man had told them.

His mama was very sad too. But she put her arms around him and said, "It's ok, my love. We will make a new picture together."

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. He lived in an old nest at the top of a tall tree. But one day, he heard a voice calling for help. It was coming from far away.

So the bird flew off to rescue the voice. He flew and he flew until he reached a lake. There, he saw a small puppy. The puppy had fallen in the water and he couldn't get out.

The bird felt sorry for the puppy, so he swooped down and used his wings to scoop the puppy out of the water. The puppy was so happy. He was spoiled and glad to be safe.

The bird flew the puppy back to the tall tree. From the top of the tree, the puppy could see his mommy and daddy on the other side of the lake. He shouted and waved to them and they waved back.

The bird flew away, into the sky, feeling very happy that he had been able to rescue the puppy and help him find his family.

In the garden, he ran and played. He chased the butterflies and the caterpillars. Then, he found the biggest tree he had ever seen. He climbed to the top and sat down. From up there, he could see the whole garden and beyond.

Tommy was so happy that he had found the secret pass. He watched the sun set, feeling peaceful and content. The garden was his happy place, a place he could go when he wanted to wander and explore.

One day Bob and Joe went to the beach together. The tide was rolling in and out, in and out. Joe wanted to go swimming, so he put on his swimming suit and jumped into the sea! But, the tide was too strong. Bob grabbed Joe's hand and zipped him back to shore.

Joe was glad to be back on the beach. He took off his swimming suit, put on his sandy shoes, and said to Bob, "Thank you for zipping me back to the beach! Shall we go and explore?"

And so, the two friends went exploring, searching for shells and watching the waves roll in and out. They were glad to have each other by their side!

Ramya made a big rocket ship with her new equipment. Each day, she would add something new to make it look just like the ones she had seen pictures of. After a few days, her rocket ship was ready!

On the day she was ready to go, Ramya dreamed even bigger. She imagined flying up in her new rocket ship to the moon. It was going to be so exciting! 

She waved goodbye and blasted off! Ramya had a wonderful trip to the moon and back. She couldn't wait to tell everyone about it when she got back.

Once upon a time, there was a very famous leopard. His name was Leo and everyone loved to play with him. He lived in the jungle and all the animals there loved him too.

Every morning Leo and his friends woke up and had lots of fun playing hide-and-seek. Then they would all run around and try to catch each other, laughing and meowing as they went. 

One day, something unexpected happened. Leo got lost and he couldn't find his way home. Everyone was very worried. They all missed Leo very much.

Luckily, one of the other leopards had a good idea! He thought they should all put their noses in the air and sniff to find him. So everyone put their noses in the air and sniffed.

Sure enough, after a few minutes of sniffing, they all smelled Leo! He was smiling in a nearby tree, and was so happy to see everyone again. Then everyone cheered for Leo and gave him a big hug. They were so glad he was safe and back with them again.

Jenny was so happy for the holiday! It was her very first holiday and she was so excited. Every morning, she woke up early and grabbed her special holiday hat. She thought it was so fun and spun around and around.

The day before the holiday, Jenny noticed her mom and dad were busy. They were carrying boxes and bags around and wrapping presents. Jenny was so curious. She asked her mom what they were doing and she explained they were getting ready for the holiday. Jenny was so happy and excited, she couldn't wait to see what the holiday was like.

On the holiday, Jenny opened her gifts and was so surprised. All of her gifts were so thoughtful and special. She grabbed a new stuffed animal and hugged it tight. Later that day, Jenny and her parents went out to pick up some food to have a special holiday dinner. When they got home, they set up the table and enjoyed a delicious meal together as a family. 

Jenny was so happy for the holiday. It was a day that she would always remember.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny fish called Tuna. Tuna was swimming in the ocean, looking for food. Suddenly, he saw a big cave. Tuna swam and swam until he reached the entrance to the cave and peered inside.

It was very dark. Tuna took a deep breath and cautiously swam in. As Tuna explored the cave he heard a loud noise. He realised that it was coming from a big door. He shivered as the door shut behind him. He was helpless.

Tuna swam around for what felt like forever, looking for a way out, but he couldn't find one. Suddenly he heard a noise coming from a corner of the cave. He swam over to investigate and found a small, glowing light. It was a magic portal!

Tuna swam through the portal and it shut behind him. Moments later, he was swimming in the bright blue ocean with the sun shining down on him. He had escaped from the dark cave and was free once more!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was a happy, spoiled boy who loved to go on adventures.

One day, Tom decided to go to the park. He got dressed and walked outside. When he got to the park, he saw a switch on the ground. He had never seen a switch before.

Tom wanted to know what would happen if he pulled the switch. He knew it was a little bit naughty, but he thought it was worth it. So he pulled the switch and waited.

Nothing happened at first. But then, Tom saw a big, old tree start to shake. A few seconds later, the tree creaked, and suddenly a door appeared in the side of the tree!

Tom was so amazed. He went up to the door and opened it. Inside, there was a big room filled with toys!

Tom was so excited. He had an amazing adventure that day and learned that a spoiled little boy can still have fun, even without having to leave the park.

Once upon a time there was a proud little girl. She was playing in the park with her friends. She saw an ash slide and was so excited to try it!

The girl stood at the top of the slide and felt so proud. She was ready to go. She took a deep breath and took off sliding down. Faster and faster she went until she reached the bottom.

The girl was grinning from ear to ear. She slid down again and again. Each time she was up there, she felt more and more proud.

Finally, the girl was exhausted from all the sliding. She waved goodbye to her friends and went home with a big smile on her face. She had had so much fun!

She picked it up and whispered to it, "What's your secret?" Suddenly, she heard an answer, "I can make you healthy!" Lucy was so excited. She quickly put the pieces of the puzzle together. When she finished, the puzzle glowed and Lucy felt better. She knew that the puzzle had magic powers that made her healthy. From then on, she took care of the puzzle and whispered to it every day.

Once upon a time there was a guard who was very enthusiastic about his job. Every day he would dress in his uniform which included a blue cap and shiny buttons. He loved to make sure that everything was safe and in order. No one ever felt scared when the guard was around.

One day, something unexpected happened. A huge, bright dragon suddenly flew around the village. Everyone was surprised, including the guard! He was so excited that he wanted to help the dragon. He ran to his house and put on his armour and sword. He became an even more enthusiastic guard.

The dragon happily flew around the village with the guard following closely behind. The guard made sure that no one was in danger and that the dragon did not create any chaos. The dragon looked so happy, it seemed as if he knew the guard was helping him.

The guard and the dragon continued to fly for the whole day, finally stopping when the sun began to set. They both said their goodbyes and the guard returned to his house to change out of his armour. The guard felt very satisfied with his day, since he had done his job so well.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the field near their house. The field has many flowers and trees and birds. Ben and Mia like to run and jump and laugh in the field.

One day, Ben and Mia find a big box in the field. The box is brown and has a hole on one side. Ben and Mia are curious. They want to see what is in the box.

"Let's use the box as a house!" Ben says. He crawls into the hole and looks inside. The box is empty and dark. "It is cozy in here!" Ben says.

"Can I come in too?" Mia asks. She tries to crawl into the hole, but she is too big. She gets stuck and cannot move. "Help! I don't fit!" Mia says.

Ben hears Mia and crawls out of the box. He sees Mia's legs and feet sticking out of the hole. He pulls Mia and helps her get out of the box. "Are you okay?" Ben asks.

Mia nods and rubs her head. "I'm okay, but the box is too small for me. I don't like the box." Mia says.

Ben and Mia look at the box and decide to leave it alone. They run and jump and laugh in the field again. They like the field more than the box. The field is big and bright and fun.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big red truck with a loud noise. It was an emergency truck. It was going to help someone who was hurt.

"Look, mom, an emergency truck!" Lily said.

"Yes, dear, it is. I hope everyone is okay," mom said.

Tom wanted to see the truck better. He ran to the road without looking. A car was coming fast. It honked its horn. Tom was scared. He screamed.

"Tom, stop!" mom shouted. She ran after him and grabbed him. She hugged him tight. "You are safe, my love. You have to be careful. The road is dangerous. You have to look both ways before you cross."

"I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I didn't see the car," Tom said. He was crying.

"It's okay, Tom. I'm glad you are not hurt. But you have to listen to me and follow the rules. They are for your own good," mom said.

She took Lily and Tom back to the park. She gave them some cookies and juice. They were delicious. Lily and Tom said thank you and sorry to mom. They ate their snacks and played some more. They were happy and safe. They learned a lesson. They loved their mom.

Anna liked to play outside with her friends. They liked to run, jump, and slide on the grass. But today, it was cold and windy. Anna's mom said, "You need to wear a sweater if you want to go outside."

Anna did not like sweaters. They were itchy and tight. She wanted to wear her pink dress with flowers. She said, "No, mom, I don't want a sweater. I want my dress."

Mom shook her head. "No, Anna, your dress is not warm enough. You will catch a cold. You have to wear a sweater. You can choose which one you like."

Anna looked at her closet. She saw a blue sweater, a green sweater, and a yellow sweater. She did not like any of them. She said, "Mom, I don't like these sweaters. They are ugly and boring. I want a pretty and fun sweater."

Mom smiled. She said, "I have a surprise for you. Look, I made you a new sweater. It is pink and has flowers on it. Just like your dress. Do you like it?"

Anna's eyes lit up. She said, "Wow, mom, you are so smart. You made me a sweater that looks like my dress. I love it. Thank you, mom. Can I wear it now?"

Mom nodded. She said, "Yes, you can wear it now. But you have to put on your coat and hat too. It is still cold outside. And don't forget to come back in time for lunch."

Anna hugged mom. She said, "OK, mom, I will. You are the best mom ever. I will show my friends my new sweater. They will like it too."

Anna put on her new sweater, her coat, and her hat. She ran outside to join her friends. They all said, "Wow, Anna, you have a nice sweater. It is pretty and fun. Where did you get it?"

Anna said, "My mom made it for me. She is so smart. She knows what I like. She permits me to wear it outside. Do you want to play with me?"

They all said, "Yes, we do. You are lucky to have such a smart mom. And such a nice sweater. Let's play together."

Sam and Lily wanted to watch a movie. They liked movies with animals and songs. They asked Mom if they could watch a movie on the big screen.

Mom said, "Yes, you can watch a movie, but first you have to tidy your room. Your room is very messy. You have toys and books and clothes everywhere. You have to put them away in the right places."

Sam and Lily did not want to tidy their room. They wanted to watch the movie now. They said, "Mom, please, can we watch the movie first and tidy our room later?"

Mom said, "No, you have to tidy your room first. That is the rule. If you don't tidy your room, you can't watch the movie. I will give you ten minutes to tidy your room. Then I will come and check. If your room is tidy, you can watch the movie. If your room is not tidy, you can't watch the movie. Do you understand?"

Sam and Lily nodded. They did not like the rule, but they wanted to watch the movie. They went to their room and started to tidy it. They put their toys in the toy box, their books on the shelf, and their clothes in the closet. They worked fast and hard. They wanted to finish in ten minutes.

Mom came to check their room. She saw that their room was tidy. She smiled and said, "Good job, Sam and Lily. You tidied your room very well. You followed the rule. Now you can watch the movie. What movie do you want to watch?"

Sam and Lily said, "We want to watch the movie with the lion and the zebra and the giraffe. They go on an adventure and sing funny songs. We like that movie."

Mom said, "Okay, let's watch that movie. Come on, let's go to the big screen. I will make some popcorn for us. Do you want some popcorn?"

Sam and Lily said, "Yes, please, we want some popcorn. Thank you, Mom. You are the best."

They went to the big screen and watched the movie. They laughed and sang along with the animals. They enjoyed the movie and the popcorn. They were happy. They were glad they tidied their room. They learned that following the rule was good. They hugged Mom and said, "We love you, Mom. Thank you for the movie and the popcorn." Mom hugged them back and said, "I love you too, Sam and Lily. You are good children. You make me proud." They snuggled together and watched the movie until the end. They had a good time.

Lily likes to draw with crayons. She has many colors of crayons in her box. She likes to draw flowers, stars, and rainbows on her paper. She draws every day after lunch.

One day, she hears a loud noise outside. She looks out the window and sees a big truck. The truck is clear and shiny. It has a long hose and a ladder. Lily wonders what the truck is doing.

She hears a man say, "We are here to wash the windows. They are very dirty and we need to make them clear and shiny." Lily sees the man climb the ladder and spray water on the windows. She sees the water make bubbles and run down the glass.

Lily thinks the truck and the water are fun. She wants to draw them with her crayons. She runs to her box and picks a clear crayon and a blue crayon. She draws the truck and the water on her paper. She shows her mom and says, "Look, mom, I draw a clear truck and water. They wash the windows and make them clear and shiny." Mom smiles and says, "That's a very good drawing, Lily. You are very clever with your crayons." Lily feels happy and proud. She likes to draw with crayons.

Lily and Tom were brother and sister. They liked to play hide and seek in the house. One day, they decided to play in the kitchen. Lily was the seeker and Tom was the hider.

Tom looked for a good place to hide. He saw a big jar of butter on the counter. He thought it would be a fun place to hide. He opened the jar and climbed inside. He closed the lid and waited for Lily to find him.

Lily counted to ten and started to look for Tom. She looked under the table, behind the chairs, in the cabinets, but she could not find him. She started to feel anxious. She called out, "Tom, where are you? I give up!"

Tom heard Lily's voice, but he did not answer. He was having too much fun hiding in the butter. He felt the butter around him, soft and warm. He smiled and giggled.

But then, he realized he could not breathe. The butter was too thick and sticky. He tried to push the lid open, but it was too heavy. He tried to scream, but no one heard him. He felt scared and sad. He wished he had not hidden in the butter.

Lily looked everywhere, but she could not find Tom. She started to cry. She ran to their mom and told her she could not find Tom. Mom was worried. She asked Lily where they were playing. Lily said they were playing in the kitchen.

Mom and Lily ran to the kitchen. They saw the jar of butter on the counter. Mom had a bad feeling. She opened the jar and saw Tom inside. He was not moving. He was not breathing. He was covered in butter. Mom screamed and cried. Lily screamed and cried.

They called for help, but it was too late. Tom was gone. He had hidden in the butter and died. Mom and Lily were very sad. They wished they had not played hide and seek in the kitchen. They wished they had listened to the rule: never play with food.

The moral of the story is: never play with food. It can be dangerous and wasteful. Food is for eating, not for hiding. Always follow the rules and be careful when you play.

Tim and Mia liked to play with their vehicles. They had cars, trucks, buses and trains. They made noises and moved them around the floor. They had fun.

One day, Tim saw a new vehicle in Mia's room. It was big and colorful. It had wheels, wings and a propeller. It was a plane. Tim wanted to play with it.

"Can I have the plane?" Tim asked Mia.

"No, it is mine. Mom gave it to me. You have your own vehicles." Mia said.

"But I like the plane. It is so colorful. Please, let me have it." Tim begged.

"No, no, no. Go away." Mia said.

Tim got angry. He tried to grab the plane from Mia. Mia held it tight. They pulled and pushed. They started to yell.

"Mine, mine, mine!" Mia yelled.

"Give, give, give!" Tim yelled.

Mom heard the yelling. She came to Mia's room. She saw Tim and Mia fighting over the plane. She was not happy.

"Stop, stop, stop!" Mom yelled. "What are you doing? Why are you yelling?"

Tim and Mia stopped. They looked at Mom. They felt sorry.

"We are sorry, Mom. We wanted to play with the plane. We both like it. It is so colorful." Tim and Mia said.

Mom smiled. She hugged them. She said, "I understand. The plane is very nice. But you have to share. You have to take turns. You have to be kind. You have to use your words, not your yelling."

Tim and Mia nodded. They said, "OK, Mom. We will share. We will take turns. We will be kind. We will use our words, not our yelling."

Mom gave them the plane. She said, "You can play with it together. But first, say sorry to each other."

Tim and Mia said sorry to each other. They hugged. They thanked Mom. They played with the plane. They made noises and moved it around the air. They had fun.

One day, they find a gray hat in their closet. It is big and soft. They think it is funny. They want to put it on Lily.

"Can we put the hat on Lily?" Sara asks Ben.

Ben nods. He likes the idea. He helps Sara put the hat on Lily. They laugh. Lily looks silly.

They take Lily to show Mom. Mom is in the kitchen. She is making lunch.

"Look, Mom, look!" Sara and Ben say. "We have a new sister. Her name is Lily. She has a gray hat."

Mom smiles. She sees Lily with the gray hat. She thinks it is cute.

"Hello, Lily," Mom says. "You have a very nice hat. Did Sara and Ben give it to you?"

Sara and Ben nod. They are proud. They hug Lily.

Mom hugs them too. She says, "You are very good twins. You are very good to Lily. You can keep the hat for her. But first, let's have some lunch. Are you hungry?"

Sara and Ben nod. They are hungry. They take Lily to the table. They share their lunch with her. They are happy. They love their baby doll. They love their gray hat. They love their Mom.

It was time for bed, but Lily did not want to sleep. She wanted to play with her toys and read her books. She yawned and rubbed her eyes, but she still said, "No, Mommy, no bed!"

Mommy smiled and said, "Lily, you are very tired. You need to sleep and have sweet dreams. Come on, let's go to your room and I will tell you a story."

Lily pouted and said, "But I want to stay with you and Daddy. Can I watch you cook on the stove?"

Mommy shook her head and said, "No, Lily, the stove is hot and dangerous. You cannot touch it or go near it. You can watch me cook tomorrow, okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mommy. But can you tell me a story about the stove?"

Mommy laughed and said, "Sure, Lily. I will tell you a story about the stove. But first, you have to brush your teeth and put on your pajamas."

Lily agreed and did what Mommy said. Then she followed Mommy to her room and climbed into her bed. Mommy tucked her in and kissed her forehead. She said, "Are you ready for the story?"

Lily said, "Yes, Mommy. Please tell me the story."

Mommy said, "Okay, Lily. Listen carefully. Once upon a time, there was a stove that lived in a kitchen. The stove was very gentle and kind. He liked to cook delicious food for the people who lived in the house. He made soup and bread and cake and pie. He made the house warm and cozy. He was very happy. But one day, he felt lonely. He wanted to have a friend. He looked around the kitchen and saw a fridge, a toaster, a kettle, and a blender. But they were all busy and did not talk to him. He felt sad and wished he had someone to talk to. Then he saw a little mouse. The mouse was hungry and looking for food. The stove felt sorry for the mouse and said, 'Hello, little mouse. Are you hungry? I have some food for you. Come and see.' The mouse was scared and said, 'Who are you? Are you going to hurt me?' The stove said, 'No, no, I am not going to hurt you. I am a stove. I cook food for the people. But they are not here now. They are sleeping. I have some food left over. You can have some if you want. I just want to be your friend.' The mouse was curious and said, 'Really? You want to be my friend? You are not like the other stoves I have seen. They are loud and scary and chase me away. You are gentle and quiet and nice. Thank you for the food. Can I stay with you for a while?' The stove said, 'Of course, you can stay with me. I am glad you are here. You can tell me stories and I will tell you stories. We can be friends.' The mouse said, 'Okay, that sounds good. You are a very kind stove. What is your name?' The stove said, 'My name is Sam. What is your name?' The mouse said, 'My name is Max. Nice to meet you, Sam.' And so, Sam the stove and Max the mouse became friends. They shared food and stories and laughter. They kept each other company and made each other happy. They were not lonely anymore. They were the best of friends. The end."

Lily smiled and said, "That was a very nice story, Mommy. I like Sam and Max. They are good friends. Can I be their friend too?"

Mommy said, "Sure, Lily. You can be their friend too. But now, you have to close your eyes and go to sleep. Tomorrow, you can play and read and watch me cook. Good night, Lily. I love you."

Lily said, "Good night, Mommy. I love you too." She closed her eyes and cuddled her teddy bear. She felt warm and cozy and happy. She fell asleep and had sweet dreams.

Tim was a spoiled boy. He always wanted new toys and candy. He did not like to share or say thank you. One day, he saw his dad's wallet on the table. He wanted to buy more things with the money inside.

He took the wallet and ran to his room. He opened it and saw many green papers. He did not know how much they were worth, but he thought they were a lot. He felt happy and greedy. He decided to mark the papers with his crayons. He drew stars and hearts and smiley faces on them. He thought they looked pretty.

But his dad was looking for his wallet. He heard Tim giggling in his room. He went to see what he was doing. He was shocked and angry when he saw the marked papers. He yelled at Tim and took the wallet away. He told him he was very naughty and he had to say sorry. He also told him he had to work hard to earn money, not waste it.

Tim felt scared and sad. He realized he had done a bad thing. He did not want to make his dad mad. He said sorry and hugged his dad. He asked him to forgive him. His dad was still upset, but he loved Tim. He told him he forgave him, but he had to learn his lesson. He said he would not buy him any new toys or candy for a long time. He also said he had to help him with chores around the house.

Tim agreed and nodded. He felt sorry for what he had done. He wanted to be a good boy. He learned that money was not for playing, but for buying things you need. He also learned that being spoiled was not good, but being grateful and kind was. He hugged his dad again and said he loved him. His dad smiled and said he loved him too.

One day, a big boy came to the park. He saw the hoop and wanted to use it. He took the hoop from Lily and Ben and ran away. Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They wanted their hoop back.

"Hey, that's our hoop!" Lily shouted. "Give it back!"

"No, it's mine now!" the big boy said. "You can't have it!"

Lily and Ben ran after the big boy. They tried to catch him and get their hoop back. But the big boy was faster and stronger. He laughed at them and kept the hoop.

Lily and Ben felt like crying. They didn't know what to do. They wished someone would help them.

Then, they saw a jolly man walking his dog. The jolly man saw what was happening and decided to help. He whistled to his dog and pointed at the big boy. The dog ran after the big boy and barked loudly. The big boy got scared and dropped the hoop. The dog picked up the hoop and brought it back to Lily and Ben.

"Thank you, thank you!" Lily and Ben said to the jolly man and his dog. They hugged the dog and smiled at the jolly man.

"You're welcome, you're welcome!" the jolly man said. "I'm glad you got your hoop back. It's not nice to take things from others. You should share and be kind."

Lily and Ben nodded and agreed. They learned a lesson that day. They thanked the jolly man and his dog again and went back to play with their hoop. They were happy and grateful. They had a lot of fun with the hoop.

Sam liked to play in the garden. He liked to look for bugs and flowers and rocks. One day, he saw a lizard on the wall. It was green and brown and had a long tail. Sam wanted to touch it.

"Hello, lizard," he said. "Can I be your friend?"

The lizard looked at Sam with its small eyes. It did not say anything. It moved its head up and down.

Sam reached out his hand to pet the lizard. But the lizard was lively. It ran away from Sam and jumped to another wall.

"Wait, lizard, don't leave!" Sam cried. He ran after the lizard. He wanted to catch it and hold it.

But the lizard was too fast and too smart. It hid behind a bush and then ran to the fence. Sam could not see it anymore.

"Where are you, lizard?" Sam asked. He looked around the garden. He felt sad. He wanted to play with the lizard.

Then he heard a voice behind him.

"Sam, it's time for lunch," his mom said. "Come inside, please."

Sam turned around and saw his mom. She smiled at him and held his hand.

"OK, mom," he said. "But can I come back later and look for the lizard?"

"Sure, Sam," his mom said. "But remember, lizards are wild animals. They don't like to be touched. They like to be free."

Sam nodded. He understood. He still liked the lizard, but he did not want to scare it. He hoped the lizard would come back and say hello to him again. He went inside with his mom and ate his lunch. He wondered what the lizard was doing.
