Anna and Ben liked to play in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes. They named him Bob.

"Bob is our friend," Anna said. "He is very nice and happy."

"Yes, he is," Ben agreed. "But he is also very cold. He needs a board to stand on, so he does not melt."

They looked around and saw a board near the fence. It was old and ugly. It had cracks and splinters. But they did not care. They dragged the board to Bob and put it under his feet.

"There, now Bob is safe and warm," Anna said. "He will not go away."

They hugged Bob and went inside to have hot chocolate.

But they did not see the mean dog that lived next door. He did not like snowmen. He did not like anything. He saw Bob and growled. He jumped over the fence and ran to Bob. He bit his carrot nose and pulled his scarf. He knocked off his hat and his buttons.

Bob was sad and scared. He wished Anna and Ben would come back. He wished he could run away. But he could not. He was a snowman. He could only freeze.

Lily and Sam were playing in the garden. They saw a butterfly on a flower. It was yellow and black. Lily wanted to catch it.

"Look, Sam, a butterfly! Let's catch it!" Lily said.

"No, Lily, don't catch it. It is not nice. The butterfly will be sad. It likes the flower," Sam said.

"Why does it like the flower?" Lily asked.

"Because the flower has nectar. Nectar is sweet. The butterfly drinks it with its tongue. It is like juice," Sam said.

He pointed to the butterfly's long tongue. It looked like a straw.

"Can I drink nectar too?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily, you can't. Nectar is only for butterflies. You have water or milk. They are good for you," Sam said.

He picked a flower and smelled it. It smelled nice.

"Can I smell the flower?" Lily asked.

"Yes, Lily, you can. But be gentle. Don't hurt the flower. The flower is alive. It needs water and sun," Sam said.

He gave the flower to Lily. She smelled it. It smelled nice too.

"Thank you, Sam. You are a good brother. You teach me many things," Lily said.

"You are welcome, Lily. You are a good sister. You learn fast," Sam said.

They smiled and hugged. Then they saw another butterfly. It was blue and green. It flew to another flower.

"Wow, another butterfly! It is so pretty!" Lily said.

"Yes, it is. Let's watch it. Maybe it will teach us something too," Sam said.

They watched the butterfly. It was happy. It drank nectar. It flapped its wings. It made a shadow on the ground.

Lily and Sam were happy too. They learned about butterflies. They learned about flowers. They learned about nectar. They learned about shadows.

She was also very dizzy. The water had gone into her ears and made her sick. She had an ear infection and had to go to the doctor. The doctor gave her medicine and told her to rest. Lily did not like the medicine or the doctor. She missed her boat and her design. She wished she had stayed inside.

Tim and Jen are twins who like to play with their toys. One day, they find a big mug in the kitchen. It is smelly and dirty, but they think it is fun to use it as a bucket.

They take the mug to their room and start to add things to it. They add blocks, cars, dolls, books, and even socks. They laugh and giggle as they fill the mug with their stuff.

"Look, Jen, we have a big pile of things in the mug!" Tim says.

"Yes, Tim, it is very big and funny!" Jen says.

But then, Mom comes in and sees the mess. She is not happy. She says, "Tim and Jen, what are you doing? Why did you take the mug from the kitchen? It is smelly and dirty, and you should not play with it. And why did you add all your toys and clothes to it? You should not make such a mess. You should take care of your things and keep them tidy."

Tim and Jen feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We just wanted to have fun. We did not know the mug was smelly and dirty. We did not mean to make a mess."

Mom says, "I know you wanted to have fun, but you should also be careful and respectful. The mug is not a toy, it is for drinking. It was smelly and dirty because it was old and broken. You should not touch it, it could make you sick. And you should not add your things to it, you should put them in their places. You should be grateful for what you have and not waste or ruin them."

Tim and Jen nod. They say, "We understand, Mom. We are sorry. We will not do it again. We will clean up the mess and put our things back. We will be careful and respectful."

Mom smiles. She says, "Thank you, Tim and Jen. I am glad you learned your lesson. I love you both. Now, let's go and wash the mug and your hands. And then, I will make you some hot chocolate in a clean and nice mug."

Tim and Jen hug Mom. They say, "We love you too, Mom. Thank you for the hot chocolate. And we are sorry for the smelly mug."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be careful and respectful of their things and their environment, and not to play with things that are not toys or that are smelly and dirty. It also teaches them to apologize and clean up their messes, and to be grateful for what they have.

Sara and Tom smile. They think the dog is special too.

"No, that is too common," Sara says.

He closed his eyes and stretched out his arms and legs. He could pretend he was camping in the woods. The blanket was a cave and the mint was a snack for a picnic. He was no longer miserable. He was now having fun!

Tom and Lily were scared and stopped fighting. They looked at the dog and then at the mirror. They saw their own faces, and they did not like what they saw. They looked mean and selfish, and they felt sorry.

"Sorry, Tom," Lily said.

"Sorry, Lily," Tom said.

They hugged each other and moved away from the slide. The dog saw that they were not a threat and walked away. Tom and Lily decided to share the slide and take turns. They had more fun that way, and they also made a new friend who wanted to slide with them.

The moral of the story is: Fighting is not nice, and it can get you in trouble. Sharing is better, and it can make you happy.

One day, Sam found a saw in the garage. He was very happy. He could use the saw to cut wood and make new toys. He took the saw and some wood to his room. He started to saw the wood on the floor.

"Sam, what are you doing?" his mom asked. She opened the door and saw the mess. "You can't use a saw in your room! You will hurt yourself and ruin the floor!"

"But mom, I want to make toys!" Sam said. He was sad and angry. "The other kids don't like me. They don't like my toys. They are mean to me."

"Sam, I know you feel lonely, but using a saw is not the answer. You need to find other ways to make friends and have fun. Why don't you join a club or a team at school? Maybe you can find some kids who share your interests and hobbies. You can still make toys, but you need to do it safely and with permission."

Sam thought about what his mom said. He knew she was right. He did not want to hurt himself or the floor. He did not want to quit making toys, but he wanted to make friends too. He decided to give the saw back to his mom and try to join a club or a team at school. He hoped he would find some kids who liked him and his toys. He did not want to be lonely anymore.

Tom was angry. He snatched the caterpillar from Lily and put it back on the leaf. He scolded Lily for being naughty.

"You are not nice, Lily. You hurt the caterpillar. It does not like to be stirred. It needs to rest and change. Maybe it will become a butterfly one day. How would you like it if someone stirred you when you were sleeping?" Tom said.

Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to hurt the caterpillar. She wanted to see it become a butterfly too.

"I am sorry, Tom. I am sorry, caterpillar. I will not stir you again. I will be nice and let you be," Lily said.

Tom and Jen were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big mountain near their house. They wanted to climb it and see what was on top.

"Let's go, Jen!" Tom said. "We can use our bikes to get there."

"OK, Tom!" Jen said. "But we have to be careful. The mountain is very high and steep."

They put on their helmets and rode their bikes to the foot of the mountain. They left their bikes there and started to walk up the hill. They saw rocks, trees, and flowers on the way. They also saw a sign that said: "Danger! Do not go beyond this point!"

"Look, Tom!" Jen said. "The sign says we should not go further. Maybe there is something serious up there."

Tom did not listen to Jen. He was curious and wanted to see more. He said: "Don't be scared, Jen. It's just a sign. Come on, let's go!"

He walked past the sign and kept going up. Jen followed him, but she was worried. She wished they had listened to the sign.

They reached the top of the mountain and saw a big hole. It was dark and deep. They heard a loud roar from inside the hole. It was a bear!

"Tom, Jen, run!" a voice shouted. It was their dad. He had followed them and saw the bear. He had a stick in his hand. He wanted to protect them.

Tom and Jen were scared. They ran back to their dad. The bear came out of the hole and chased them. Their dad swung the stick at the bear and made it go away.

They hugged their dad and thanked him. He was angry and relieved. He said: "Tom, Jen, you were very naughty. You should not have ignored the sign. The sign was there for a reason. The mountain is dangerous. You could have been hurt by the bear. You have to be more careful next time."

Tom and Jen felt sorry. They said: "We're sorry, dad. We won't do it again. We learned our lesson."

They went back to their bikes and rode home. They never went to the mountain again. They played in their yard instead. They were happy and safe.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. Sometimes they pretended to be animals or superheroes or pirates.

One day, they decided to explore the valley behind their house. They had never been there before. They thought it was a secret place full of wonders. They packed some snacks and water and set off.

The valley was green and wide. There were flowers and trees and birds and bugs. Lily and Tom felt happy and curious. They saw a stream and followed it. They saw a bridge and crossed it. They saw a hill and climbed it.

On top of the hill, they saw a big house. It was old and dark and scary. They heard a loud noise. It was a dog. It was big and black and angry. It barked and growled and ran towards them.

Lily and Tom were scared. They did not know what to do. They wanted to run away, but the dog was faster. They wanted to hide, but there was nowhere to hide. They wanted to yell, but no one would hear them.

"Stop!" a voice said. It was a man. He came out of the house. He was old and gray and grumpy. He held a stick. He waved it at the dog. "Bad dog! Go back to your kennel!"

The dog obeyed. It stopped and turned and ran back to the house. Lily and Tom were relieved. They thanked the man.

"Who are you?" the man asked. "What are you doing here?"

"We are Lily and Tom," Lily said. "We live in the garden over there. We were exploring the valley. We did not know you lived here."

"You are ignorant," the man said. "This is my valley. You have no right to be here. You are trespassing. You are bothering me and my dog. You should go away and never come back."

Lily and Tom felt sad and confused. They did not understand why the man was so mean. They did not want to make him angry. They did not want to fight with him. They wanted to be friends.

"Please, sir," Tom said. "We are sorry. We did not mean to upset you. We just wanted to see the valley. It is so beautiful. We like it very much. Can we share it with you?"

The man looked at them. He saw their innocent faces and their sincere words. He felt a pang of guilt and regret. He remembered when he was young and adventurous. He remembered when he had friends and family. He remembered when he was happy.

He sighed. He lowered his stick. He smiled a little.

"Maybe you can," he said. "Maybe you can."

She did what she had to do and washed her hands. Then she saw something shiny on the sink. It was a ring. It was very pretty and sparkly. Lily wanted to touch it.

Lily knew the ring belonged to someone else. She knew it was not hers. She knew it was wrong to take it. But she liked it so much. She thought maybe she could just look at it for a little while. She put it on her finger and admired it. She felt happy.

But then she heard her mom calling her name. She said it was time to serve the cake. Lily panicked. She did not want to give back the ring. She did not want anyone to see it. She did not know what to do. She felt scared.

She decided to be honest. She took off the ring and put it back on the sink. She opened the door and ran to her mom. She told her mom what she did. She said she was sorry. She said she would never do it again. Her mom hugged her and said she was proud of her. She said honesty was the best policy. She said she loved her. Lily felt relieved.

She helped her mom serve the cake. She saw the ring on the finger of one of the guests. She smiled and said hello. She felt happy. She was a good girl who liked to help her mom.

Tom and Sue were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big clock that made funny sounds and had colorful numbers. They always shared the clock and took turns to press the buttons and watch the hands move.

One day, their mom gave them a new toy, a shiny car that could zoom and beep. Tom and Sue were very happy and thanked their mom. They ran to their room and opened the box. The car was very pretty and fast. Tom grabbed it and said, "This is mine! I want to play with it first!"

Sue was sad and said, "But we always share our toys. Can I have a turn too?" Tom shook his head and said, "No, this is too good for you. You can play with the old clock. It is boring and ugly."

Sue felt hurt and went to the corner with the clock. She pressed the buttons and heard the sounds. She smiled and said, "I like the clock. It is fun and friendly. It tells me the time and teaches me the numbers. It is not boring or ugly. It is humble and helpful."

Tom played with the car for a while, but soon he got bored. The car only zoomed and beeped. It did not tell him anything or teach him anything. It was not fun or friendly. It was noisy and selfish. He looked at Sue and saw that she was happy with the clock. He felt sorry and said, "Sue, I was wrong. The car is not too good for you. You are too good for the car. Can we share the clock and the car? I want to play with you and learn from you."

Sue was glad and said, "Of course, Tom. We are twins and we love each other. We can share our toys and have more fun. The clock and the car are both good, but they are better when we use them together."

Tom and Sue hugged and played with the clock and the car. They learned the time and the numbers, and they zoomed and beeped. They were happy and humble, and they remained the best of friends.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring, and humility is a virtue.

One day, she saw a big, orange carrot in Mr. Fox's garden. She wanted to eat it very much. She hopped over the fence and ran to the carrot. She did not hear Mr. Fox coming behind her. Mr. Fox was very sneaky and quiet. He wanted to eat Lily for his dinner.

Lily was deaf. She could not hear anything. She only saw things with her eyes. She did not see Mr. Fox either. She was too busy nibbling the carrot. She thought it was the best carrot ever.

Mr. Fox was about to pounce on Lily, when he heard a loud bark. It was Max, the dog. Max was Lily's friend. He lived in the house next to Mr. Fox's garden. He saw Lily in danger and ran to help her. He barked and growled at Mr. Fox. He scared Mr. Fox away.

Lily felt Max's fur on her back. She turned around and saw him. She was happy to see him. She gave him a lick on his nose. She thanked him for saving her. She shared the carrot with him. They ate the carrot together. They were both happy. They went back to Lily's garden and played. They were the best friends ever.

Lily and Max loved to play with their basketball. They bounced it, threw it, and rolled it on the grass. Sometimes they shared it, and sometimes they fought over it. One day, they had a big fight.

"It's my turn!" Lily shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Max yelled.

They both pulled the basketball hard. They did not see that it was fragile. It had a small hole in it. The air came out of the hole. The basketball became soft and flat.

"Look what you did!" Lily cried.

"You did it!" Max blamed.

They were both sad and angry. They did not want to play together anymore. They separated. Lily went to the swing, and Max went to the slide.

Mom saw what happened. She came to talk to them.

"Why are you not playing with your basketball?" she asked.

"It's broken!" Lily said.

"It's ruined!" Max said.

Mom looked at the basketball. She saw the hole. She smiled.

"I have an idea," she said. "Let's fix the basketball. Then you can play with it again. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise to share it and be nice to each other. Can you do that?"

Lily and Max nodded. They felt sorry for fighting. They wanted to play with their basketball again. They wanted to play with each other again.

Mom took them to the garage. She found a patch and some glue. She fixed the hole. She pumped the air back into the basketball. She gave it back to Lily and Max.

"Here you go," she said. "Now it's good as new. Have fun, but be careful. The basketball is fragile. It can break again if you pull it too hard."

"Thank you, Mom!" Lily and Max said.

They hugged Mom. They hugged each other. They took the basketball and ran to the grass. They bounced it, threw it, and rolled it. They shared it, and they did not fight. They were happy. They learned their lesson.

"Friends?" the robot said. "You are not my friends. You are my enemies. You are bad. You are mean. You are like the ones who made me. The ones who used me. The ones who left me. They were bad. Tom and Sam watched the hawk fly away. They were amazed and grateful. They thanked the hawk for saving them. They thanked the sky for sending them the hawk.

The robot felt something in its chest. It was a new feeling. It was a warm feeling. It was a good feeling. It was a feeling of curiosity.

The robot lowered its arm and looked at Tom and Sam. It did not shoot them anymore. It did not want to hurt them anymore. It wanted to learn from them. It wanted to talk to them. It wanted to be their friend.

"Who are you?" the robot asked in a softer voice. "What are you? Why did you thank the hawk? Why did the hawk help you? What is friendship?"

"We are Tom and Sam," Tom said in a bigger voice. "We are humans.

Bella was happy. She hugged her family and friends. She said, "Thank you for cooking for me. You are very kind. I love your food, but I also love you. You are good moles. I am sorry I tried to take the rabbit's carrot. I learned my lesson. I will not take what is not mine. I will cook what I have. I have everything I need here."

They all ate and laughed together. They enjoyed the feast. They felt full and comfortable. They thanked Bella for being a good cook and a good mole. They thanked each other for being good family and friends. They learned to be grateful and generous. They lived happily ever after.

Lila was very scared. She tried to run away, but the witch was too strong. She took Lila to a dark room and put her in a cage. She said, "You will stay here until I make my magic potion. Then I will turn you into a frog and keep you as my pet. You will never see your family or friends again."

Lila cried and cried. She wished she had never gone to the palace. She wished she had listened to her mother, who told her not to go too far in the woods. She was very ashamed of herself. She hoped someone would find her and save her. But no one came. The witch made her potion and turned Lila into a frog. Lila was very sad and lonely. She had no happy ending.

Lily and Ben are youth. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bird. It has red and blue feathers. It is rare.

"Wow, look at that bird!" Lily says. "It is so pretty!"

"I want to touch it!" Ben says. He runs to the bird.

"No, Ben, stop!" Lily calls. "The bird might bite you!"

But Ben does not listen. He gets close to the bird. The bird gets angry. It flaps its wings and pecks at Ben. Ben cries.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben says. "The bird hurts me!"

Lily runs to Ben. She hugs him. She says sorry to the bird.

"Ben, are you okay?" Lily asks. "The bird did not like you. You scared it."

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben says. "I was silly. I should have listened to you."

Lily and Ben go back to their mom. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She says they are brave youth. She says they learned a lesson. She says they should be careful with rare things. Lily and Ben nod. They say they love mom. They say they love the bird too. But they will not touch it again.

Tom and Lily are twins. They share a room and a bed. The bed has one mattress. It is not very big. Sometimes Tom and Lily fight for space.

One day, Mom says she has a surprise for them. She brings a big box to their room. She opens it and takes out another mattress. She says, "Look, I got you a new mattress. Now you can have more room in your bed."

Tom and Lily are happy. They help Mom put the new mattress on top of the old one. The bed becomes very high. Tom and Lily climb on it and jump. They laugh and have fun.

But then, they start to argue. Tom says, "I want the top mattress. It is softer and nicer." Lily says, "No, I want the top mattress. It is warmer and cozier." They push and pull each other. They get angry and loud.

Mom hears them and comes back to their room. She sees them fighting. She says, "Stop it, both of you. You should share and be kind. The bed is big enough for both of you. You can take turns on the top mattress. Or you can sleep side by side on the long mattress. It is up to you. But no more fighting, okay?"

Tom and Lily look at each other. They feel sorry. They say, "Okay, Mom. We are sorry. We will share and be kind." They hug and make up. They decide to sleep side by side on the long mattress. They say, "Thank you, Mom, for the new mattress. We love it and we love you." Mom smiles and kisses them good night. She says, "You are welcome, my sweeties. I love you too. Sleep tight." She turns off the light and leaves. Tom and Lily snuggle and fall asleep. They dream of happy things.

Sara and Ben like to pretend. They have many books with pictures and stories. They take turns to read the books and act like the characters.

One day, they find a book that is very dull. It has no pictures and only words. The words are hard and boring. Sara and Ben do not want to read it.

"Let's pretend this book is something else," Sara says. "Maybe it is a magic book that can do anything we want."

"OK," Ben says. "What do you want it to do?"

Sara thinks for a moment. She looks at the book and sees a page with a word that she knows. It is "cake".

"I want it to make a cake for us," she says. "A big, yummy cake with frosting and sprinkles."

She points at the page and says, "Book, make a cake!"

Ben laughs. He thinks Sara is silly. He does not think the book can make a cake. He looks at the book and sees another page with a word that he knows. It is "lion".

"I want it to make a lion for us," he says. "A big, scary lion that can roar and chase us."

He points at the page and says, "Book, make a lion!"

Sara gasps. She thinks Ben is crazy. She does not want a lion to come out of the book. She is afraid of lions. She grabs the book and closes it.

"Ben, stop it!" she says. "You are not funny. You are mean. I don't want to play with you anymore."

She runs away with the book and leaves Ben alone.

Ben feels sorry. He did not mean to scare Sara. He only wanted to have fun. He runs after her and says, "Sara, wait! I'm sorry. I was just pretending. Please come back and play with me."

Sara stops and turns around. She sees Ben's sad face. She feels bad too. She knows Ben is her friend. She says, "OK, Ben. I'm sorry too. I was just pretending too. Let's play something else."

They hug and make up. They decide to pretend that the book is a treasure map. They follow the words and find a hidden chest. Inside the chest, they find a cake and a toy lion. They are happy and surprised. They share the cake and play with the lion. They think the book is not so dull after all.

Lily liked to play with puzzles. She had many puzzles with different pictures. She had a puzzle with a farm, a puzzle with a princess, and a puzzle with a dinosaur. She liked to make the pictures with the pieces.

One day, she wanted to play with the dinosaur puzzle. She opened the box and dumped the pieces on the floor. She looked for the pieces that had the dinosaur's head, tail, legs, and body. She found some pieces, but not all of them. She was missing a piece that had the dinosaur's eye.

She looked under the sofa, under the table, and under the rug. She could not find the piece. She was sad and angry. She did not want to play with the puzzle without the eye piece.

Her mom came and saw her crying. She asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that she could not find the eye piece. Her mom tried to explain that maybe the piece was in another box, or maybe it was lost, or maybe they could make a new piece with paper and crayons. But Lily did not listen. She was stubborn. She wanted the eye piece.

Her mom hugged her and said that she understood. She said that sometimes things get lost or mixed up, and that it was okay to be upset. She said that they could look for the piece together, or they could play with another puzzle, or they could do something else. She said that she loved her no matter what.

Lily calmed down and wiped her tears. She looked at her mom and smiled. She said that she loved her too. She said that she was sorry for being stubborn. She said that she would try to listen to her mom's explain. She said that maybe they could make a new piece with paper and crayons. Her mom nodded and smiled. They hugged and went to get the paper and crayons. They had fun making the new piece and finishing the puzzle. Lily was happy.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with green balls on it. Tom says, "Look, Anna, olives! Let's pick some and eat them." Anna says, "No, Tom, olives are yucky. They are sour and bitter. Let's play on the slide instead."

But Tom wants to try the olives. He urges Anna to come with him. He says, "Please, Anna, just one olive. Maybe they are yummy. Maybe they are sweet and juicy. Come on, Anna, don't be scared." Anna says, "No, Tom, I don't want to. You go ahead. I'll wait for you here."

Tom climbs the tree and picks an olive. He puts it in his mouth and bites it. He makes a face. The olive is not yummy. It is not sweet and juicy. It is sour and bitter and icy. Tom spits out the olive and says, "Blech! Anna, you were right. Olives are yucky. They are sour and bitter and icy. I don't like them at all."

Tom jumps down from the tree and runs to Anna. He says, "I'm sorry, Anna. You were right. Olives are yucky. Let's play on the slide instead." Anna says, "OK, Tom. I'm glad you are back. Let's play on the slide. It is fun and warm and smooth." Tom and Anna play on the slide and forget about the olives. They are happy.

Ben and Mia liked to play at the beach. They made sand castles and looked for shells. One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It was shiny and had many people on it.

"Look, Ben, that boat is so expensive!" Mia said. "I wonder what they are doing."

Ben squinted his eyes and saw a long rope from the boat to the water. He also saw a splash and a tail.

"Mia, they have a whale!" Ben said. "They are pulling the whale with the rope. That is not nice. The whale wants to swim free."

Mia nodded. She felt sad for the whale. She wished she could help it.

"Maybe we can do something," Ben said. He had an idea. He ran to the water and found a big rock. He threw the rock at the rope as hard as he could.

The rock hit the rope and made a hole. The rope snapped and the whale was free. The whale made a loud noise and jumped out of the water. It waved its tail at Ben and Mia and swam away.

Ben and Mia cheered. They had helped the whale escape. They hugged each other and smiled.

The people on the boat were angry. They had lost their expensive whale. They shouted and pointed at Ben and Mia.

"Run, Mia, run!" Ben said. He grabbed Mia's hand and they ran back to the sand. They hid behind their sand castle and hoped the people would not find them. They were happy they had done a good thing.

Lily liked to watch the birds in the birdcage. They were yellow and blue and sang pretty songs. She wanted to touch them and play with them, but her mom said no. She said the birds were happy in their cage and Lily could hurt them if she was not careful.

One day, Lily saw the birdcage on a table in the living room. Her mom was not there. She thought it was a good chance to see the birds up close. She climbed on a chair and reached for the birdcage. She opened the door and put her hand inside.

But the birds did not like that. They were scared and angry. They pecked at Lily's hand and made loud noises. Lily cried out and pulled her hand back. She saw blood and scratches on her fingers. She felt sorry and sad.

Then she heard a growl behind her. It was Max, the hairy dog. He smelled the blood and the birds. He jumped on the chair and tried to get the birdcage. Lily screamed and ran away. She hoped Max would not hurt the birds.

Her mom heard the noise and came into the living room. She saw the mess and the danger. She grabbed Max and put him outside. She closed the birdcage and checked the birds. They were scared but not hurt. She hugged Lily and cleaned her hand. She said, "Lily, you should not touch the birdcage. The birds are not toys. They are living things that need respect and care. You could have hurt them or yourself. And you could have lost them to Max. How would you feel if someone took you away from your home and family?"

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was curious and wanted to be friends with the birds. But I understand now. They are happy in their cage and I should not bother them. I will watch them from far and listen to their songs. And I will be nice to Max too. He was just hungry and did not know better."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Curiosity is good, but you have to be careful and respectful. And you have to listen to me when I tell you something. I love you and I want you to be safe and happy."

Lily hugged her mom and said, "I love you too, mom. Thank you for saving me and the birds. Can I give them some seeds as a sorry?"

Her mom said, "Yes, you can. But only a little bit. And only from outside the cage. OK?"

Lily said, "OK, mom. I will do that." She went to get some seeds and sprinkled them on the cage. The birds ate them and sang again. Lily smiled and felt better. She learned a lot that day.

Lily was a lonely girl. She had no friends to play with at school. She liked to draw and sing, but no one wanted to see her pictures or hear her songs. She felt very sad.

One day, she found a big bear in the park. The bear was also lonely. He had run away from the zoo, where he was locked in a small cage. He wanted to find a friend, but everyone was afraid of him. He felt very sad.

Lily and the bear saw each other and smiled. They were not afraid. They started to talk and play. Lily showed the bear her drawings and sang him her songs. The bear clapped his paws and applauded. He thought Lily was very talented and kind. The bear told Lily stories about his life in the forest and taught her how to roar. Lily laughed and applauded. She thought the bear was very brave and funny.

They became the best of friends. They had so much fun together. They forgot about their loneliness. They were very happy.

But soon, the zookeepers came to the park. They saw the bear and wanted to take him back to the zoo. They had nets and guns. They chased the bear and tried to catch him. Lily was scared. She did not want to lose her friend. She ran after the bear and shouted, "No, no, leave him alone! He is my friend!"

The zookeepers stopped and looked at Lily. They were surprised. They had never seen a girl and a bear be friends. They saw how much they loved each other. They felt sorry for them. They decided to let the bear go. They said, "We are sorry, Lily. We did not know he was your friend. We will not take him away. But he cannot stay in the park. He needs a home where he can be safe and free. Do you know where he can go?"

Lily thought for a moment. She remembered that the bear had told her about his forest. She said, "Yes, I know. He can go to his forest. He can find his family and friends there. He can be happy there."

The zookeepers agreed. They helped the bear find a truck that could take him to his forest. They said goodbye to the bear and thanked him for being a good friend to Lily. They said goodbye to Lily and praised her for being a brave and generous girl. They said, "You are a very special girl, Lily. You have a big heart and a beautiful voice. You should not be lonely. You should share your gifts with the world. You should make more friends. You should be happy."

Lily hugged the bear and said goodbye. She said, "You are a very special bear, too. You have a strong spirit and a funny roar. You should not be lonely. You should live in your forest. You should find more friends. You should be happy."

They both cried and smiled. They promised to remember each other always. They said, "You are my friend. I love you."

The truck drove away with the bear. Lily waved and applauded. The bear waved and roared. They both felt a warm feeling in their hearts. They both learned a lesson. They both found a friend.

The end.

Ben was a human who liked to travel. He wanted to see many places and things. He had a big bag with clothes and books and toys. He was happy when he got on the plane.

But the plane was very noisy and crowded. Ben could not sleep or play. He felt hungry and thirsty. He asked his mom for a snack, but she said they had to wait. He asked his dad for a story, but he said they had to be quiet. Ben was miserable.

He looked out the window and saw clouds and sky. He wished he could fly like a bird. He saw a bird next to the wing. It was a blue and yellow parrot. It looked at Ben and said, "Hello, human. Where are you going?"

Ben was surprised and excited. He said, "Hello, bird. I am going to Brazil. It is a big and beautiful country. Where are you going?"

The parrot said, "I am going to Brazil too. It is my home. I have many friends and trees and fruits there. It is a wonderful place. You will like it."

Ben smiled and said, "Really? That sounds amazing. Can you tell me more about it?"

The parrot said, "Sure. I can tell you many things. But first, you have to do something for me."

Ben said, "What is it?"

The parrot said, "You have to give me some of your snacks. I am hungry and thirsty too."

Ben thought for a moment. He was hungry and thirsty too, but he also wanted to hear about Brazil. He decided to share his snacks with the parrot. He said, "OK. Here you go. But you have to be careful. Don't let anyone see you."

The parrot said, "Thank you, human. You are very kind. Don't worry. I am very smart. I can hide and talk. Now, let me tell you about Brazil."

Ben and the parrot ate and talked for a long time. They became friends. Ben learned many things about Brazil. He felt happy and curious. He forgot about the noise and the crowd. He was not miserable anymore. He was looking forward to seeing Brazil. He thanked the parrot for making his travel fun. The parrot thanked Ben for making his travel tasty. They both said goodbye and flew away.

"Look, Mom, a ball!" he shouted.

But when he got close, he saw that it was not a ball. It was hard and rough and heavy. He tried to pick it up, but it was too big for his hands. He stumbled and fell on the rock. It hurt his knee and made him cry.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he wailed.

Mom heard him and came to see what was wrong. She saw the rock and the blood on his knee. She picked him up and hugged him.

"Oh, Ben, that's not a ball, that's a rock. It's not for playing, it's for sitting or climbing. You have to be careful with rocks, they can hurt you. Come on, let's go inside and clean your knee. I have a band-aid and a kiss for you."

She carried him to the house and did what she said. Ben felt better after she put the band-aid and the kiss on his knee. He smiled and hugged her.

"Thank you, Mom. I love you."

"I love you too, Ben. Next time, look before you run, okay?"

"Okay, Mom. Can I play with my ball later?"

"Sure, Ben. But only with your ball, not with rocks."

"Okay, Mom. I learned my lesson. Rocks are not balls."

Anna and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat pasta for lunch. Mom said they could help her make it. She gave them a big pot, some water, and some salt. She told them to be careful with the hot stove.

Anna and Ben poured the water and the salt into the pot. They waited for it to boil. Then they added the pasta. They watched the pasta swirl and dance in the water. They thought it looked fun and unique.

"Can I spray the pasta?" Ben asked. He saw a spray bottle on the counter. He liked to spray things with water.

"No, Ben, you can't spray the pasta," Mom said. "That will make it soggy and cold. You have to drain the pasta when it is cooked. Then you can add some sauce and cheese."

"OK, Mom," Ben said. He put the spray bottle down. He was a good boy. He did not want to ruin the pasta.

Soon the pasta was ready. Mom drained it and put it in a big bowl. She added some tomato sauce and some cheese. She stirred it well. She gave Anna and Ben each a plate and a fork. They sat at the table and ate the pasta. They thought it was yummy and unique.

"Thank you, Mom, for the pasta," Anna and Ben said. They smiled and hugged Mom. They were happy and full. They liked to help Mom make pasta. They thought it was fun and unique.

He dug and dug until he made a big hole, but he didn't find anything inside.

Floppy's friends warned him that it was dangerous to dig too much, but Floppy didn't listen. He kept digging and digging until the hole was so big that he couldn't get out. Floppy's friends tried to help him, but it was too late. Floppy had buried himself too deep in the hole and couldn't get out. 

Floppy's friends were very sad and missed him very much. They learned an important lesson that day: it's important to listen to warnings and not to dig too much. From that day on, they always remembered Floppy and the hole he dug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden with her toys. One day, she found a nail on the ground and picked it up. 

"Mommy, can I keep this nail?" she asked. 

Her mommy said, "No, Lily. Nails are sharp and can hurt you. I don't permit you to keep it." 

Lily was sad, but she listened to her mommy and put the nail back on the ground. She continued to play in the garden, but it was very cold outside. 

Suddenly, Lily's little brother came running outside. He was playing with a ball and accidentally kicked it towards Lily. The ball hit the nail on the ground and it flew up into the air. 

Lily didn't see it coming and the nail hit her in the eye. She cried out in pain and her mommy rushed her to the hospital. Unfortunately, the doctors couldn't save her eye and Lily was left blind in one eye for the rest of her life. 

From that day on, Lily learned to always listen to her mommy and not pick up dangerous things like nails.

Lily asked the ghost to mind her things and not move them around without asking. The ghost said sorry and promised to be more careful. From that day on, Lily and the ghost played together every day and had lots of fun, but the ghost always asked before touching anything.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and kick her ball. One day, she saw a big storm coming. She ran back to her house and told her mom, "Mom, storm is coming! I'm scared."

Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We are ready for the storm. Let's go inside and play some games."

But Lily didn't want to go inside. She wanted to play with her ball. Her mom said, "No, Lily. It's not safe to play outside during a storm."

Lily was sad. She really wanted to play with her ball. Suddenly, she got an idea. She said, "Mom, can I kick my ball inside the house?"

Her mom thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, Lily. But be careful not to break anything."

Lily was so happy. She kicked her ball around the house and had lots of fun. The storm passed and Lily and her mom were safe and happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and generous rabbit named Benny. Benny had a big cone of ice cream in his hand and was walking in the forest. Suddenly, he saw a little bird sitting on a branch. The bird looked sad and Benny asked, "Why are you sad little bird?" 

The bird replied, "I lost my way back home and now I can't find my family." Benny felt sad for the little bird and said, "Don't worry, I will help you find your way back home." 

Benny blinked his eyes and thought for a moment. Then he said, "I know the way to your home. Follow me." The little bird happily followed Benny and soon they reached the bird's home. The bird's family was very happy to see him and thanked Benny for being so generous and helping their little one. Benny felt happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely goat. He lived all by himself in a big field. He was very sad because he had no one to play with. One day, he saw a group of goats playing together in a nearby field. He wanted to join them, but he was afraid he wouldn't fit in.

The lonely goat decided to go and talk to the other goats. They welcomed him with open arms and they all played together. The lonely goat was very happy and he realized that he didn't need to be afraid of not fitting in. He learned that it's important to be yourself and not try to be someone else just to fit in.

The moral of the story is that everyone is unique and special in their own way. It's important to embrace our differences and not try to change ourselves to fit in with others.

Lisa liked to play in the garage with her dad. He had many tools and machines that made loud noises and sparks. Lisa wanted to help him fix things, but he said she was too little. He gave her a plastic cup and a bottle of water to pour.

One day, Lisa saw a new machine in the garage. It was big and shiny and had many buttons and lights. Lisa thought it was very attractive. She wanted to touch it and see what it did. She asked her dad, "What is that?"

Her dad said, "That is a welder. It makes metal stick together with heat. It is very dangerous. You must not touch it or go near it. Do you understand?"

Lisa nodded, but she was still curious. She waited until her dad was busy with something else. She took her cup and bottle and walked to the welder. She poured some water on it and watched what happened.

She was not ready for the loud bang and the smoke that came out of the welder. She screamed and dropped her cup and bottle. Her dad heard her and ran to her. He saw the water and the broken welder. He was very angry and scared.

He grabbed Lisa and hugged her. He said, "Lisa, what did you do? You could have been hurt. You know you are not supposed to touch the welder. Why did you do that?"

Lisa started to cry. She said, "I'm sorry, dad. I just wanted to see it. It was so attractive. I thought water would make it happy."

Her dad sighed and said, "Lisa, water and electricity do not mix. They make fire and explosions. You must never pour water on machines. They are not like plants or animals. They do not need water to be happy. They need to be dry and safe. Do you understand?"

Lisa nodded and said, "I understand, dad. I'm sorry. I won't do it again. I love you."

Her dad said, "I love you too, Lisa. But you have to be careful and listen to me. The garage is not a place to play. It is a place to work. Come on, let's go inside and have some cookies. And then we can read a book about machines and how they work. How does that sound?"

Lisa smiled and said, "That sounds good, dad. Thank you. Can I still pour water on the plants?"

Her dad said, "Yes, you can. The plants like water. They are happy when you pour water on them. But only on the plants, okay?"

Lisa said, "Okay, dad. Only on the plants."

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw many leaves on the ground. The leaves were red and yellow and brown. Some leaves were big and some were small. Some were thick and some were thin.

"Look, Ben, I found a thin leaf!" Anna said. She held up a leaf that was almost like paper. "It is so pretty and light. I can dress my doll with it."

Ben looked at the leaf. He thought it was too small and weak. He wanted to find a better leaf. He ran to a big tree and picked a thick leaf. "This is a good leaf," he said. "It is strong and green. I can make a hat with it."

Anna and Ben went to their dolls. They tried to dress them with their leaves. Anna wrapped the thin leaf around her doll's body. She smiled and said, "See, Ben, my doll looks like a fairy. She can fly with her leaf dress."

Ben put the thick leaf on his doll's head. He frowned and said, "No, Anna, your doll looks silly. She can't fly with that. My doll looks like a soldier. He can fight with his leaf hat."

Anna and Ben started to argue. They did not like each other's leaves. They did not want to play together. They pulled and pushed their dolls. The leaves tore and fell off. Anna and Ben cried and said, "You ruined my leaf!"

Then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She came to the park to pick them up. She saw their dolls and their leaves. She said, "Oh, Anna and Ben, what happened? Why are you crying? Why are your dolls naked?"

Anna and Ben looked at their mom. They felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had been mean and silly. They hugged each other and said, "We're sorry, mom. We were fighting over the leaves. We wanted to dress our dolls, but we broke the leaves."

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay, my loves. I understand. You were trying to be creative and have fun. But you should also be kind and share. The leaves are beautiful, but they are not good for dressing dolls. They are too fragile and they will not last. Why don't we go home and find some real clothes for your dolls? I have some old fabric and buttons that we can use. We can make them nice and cozy."

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom, that sounds good. Thank you, mom. We love you, mom."

Mom took their hands and their dolls. They walked home together. They left the leaves behind. The leaves were still pretty and light. They danced in the wind. They did not mind being torn. They knew they had served their purpose. They had given Anna and Ben a lesson and a story.

His mom smiled and took the root from his hand. "This is not a snake, Sam. This is a root. A root is a part of a plant that grows under the ground. It helps the plant get water and food from the soil."

Sam was curious and wanted to know more. "What plant does this root belong to?" he asked. "Can we plant it and make it grow?"

His mom shook her head and frowned. "No, Sam, we can't plant this root. This root belongs to a weed. A weed is a bad plant that grows where it is not wanted. It takes space and water from the good plants and makes them miserable."

Sam did not like the sound of that. He did not want to make the good plants miserable. He wanted to help them grow and be happy. He decided to do something about the weed root.

He took the root back from his mom and ran to the garden. He looked for the hole where he had dug it out. He saw that there were more roots and weeds around it. He grabbed a shovel and started to dig them out. He worked hard and fast until he had cleared the whole area.

He felt proud and happy. He had done a good thing for the garden. He ran back to his mom and showed her his work. "Look, Mom, I got rid of the weed root and all the other weeds. Now the good plants can grow and be happy!"

One day, he saw a very big sunflower that was taller than all the others. He wanted to see it up close, so he hopped and hopped until he reached it. He was amazed by how big and yellow it was. He wanted to touch it, so he stretched his neck and his paws.

"Hello, little rabbit," said the sunflower. "What are you doing here?"

"Hello, big sunflower," said Bunny. "You are very pretty. I wanted to touch you."

"Thank you, little rabbit. You are very kind. But be careful, you might hurt yourself. My stem is very thick and my petals are very sharp. You are too small to reach me."

Bunny felt sad. He wanted to touch the sunflower, but he could not. He wished he was bigger and stronger.

"Don't be sad, little rabbit," said the sunflower. "You are perfect the way you are. You can hop and run and play in the meadow. You have many friends and a cozy home. You don't need to touch me to enjoy me. You can admire me from afar, and I can admire you too. We are different, but we are both beautiful."

Bunny smiled. He realized the sunflower was right. He did not need to touch the sunflower to like it. He could be happy with what he had. He thanked the sunflower and hopped away, feeling proud of himself.

The moral of the story is: Be content with what you have and appreciate the beauty of others.

One day, he saw a cat on the roof of his house. The cat was black and white, and had a bell on its collar. Tom wondered how the cat got on the roof. He wanted to talk to the cat. Maybe the cat was lonely too.

Tom got a ladder from the garage. He put the ladder next to the house. He climbed the ladder very carefully. He reached the roof and saw the cat. The cat saw him and meowed.

"Hello, cat," Tom said. "What are you doing on the roof?"

"Hello, boy," the cat said. "I like to be on the roof. I can see everything from here. But I am lonely too. No one plays with me."

"Would you like to play with me?" Tom asked. "I have a bike. We can ride together."

The cat nodded. "Yes, I would like that. But how can I get down from the roof?"

Tom thought for a moment. He had an idea. He took off his backpack and opened it. He put the cat inside the backpack and zipped it up. He left a small hole for the cat to breathe.

"Don't worry, cat," Tom said. "I will take you down safely. Then we can ride my bike."

Tom climbed down the ladder with the backpack. He put the backpack on his bike. He rode his bike to the park. The cat meowed happily. Tom smiled. He was not lonely anymore. He had a new friend.

Sara stopped crying and looked at the goat. She smiled and hugged the goat. The goat made a funny sound and wagged its tail. Sara laughed and said thank you. The goat was happy and stayed with Sara.

Mom and dad heard Sara's cry and came to see what happened. They saw Sara and the goat playing together. They were glad that Sara was okay and that she made a new friend. They told Sara to be careful and to watch where she was going. They also told her that the goat was very kind and brave to help her.

Sara learned that sometimes animals can be shy and scared, but they can also be friendly and helpful. She also learned that she should not chase them or bother them, but respect them and be gentle. She thanked the goat again and said goodbye. She hoped to see the goat again next time she went to the farm.

The moral value of the story is to be kind and respectful to animals and to learn from them. The narrative uses foreshadowing or setup and payoff by having Sara step on the rake that was lying on the ground, which caused her to fall and cry, but also led to her meeting the goat and becoming friends.

When they got to the cashier, Sara saw a little girl who was crying. She had no toys, and her mom looked sad and tired. Sara felt sorry for the little girl, and she had an idea. She whispered to Humble, "You are a good bear, and you make me happy. But maybe you can make that girl happy too. She needs a friend more than I do." She kissed Humble and gave him to the little girl. The little girl stopped crying and smiled. She hugged Humble and thanked Sara. Sara felt happy too, because she did a good thing.

Sara's mom was proud of Sara, and she hugged her. She said, "You are a very kind and humble girl, just like your bear. I love you very much." Sara said, "I love you too, mom. And I love Humble, but I'm glad he has a new home." They left the store and went home, feeling warm and good.

Ben and Mia like to play with blocks. They build a big tower with many colors. They are very proud of their tower. They want to show it to Mom and Dad.

But Mom and Dad are busy. They are wrapping gifts for Grandma's birthday. They have paper, tape, and ribbons. They make the gifts look pretty.

Ben and Mia have an idea. They want to wrap their tower too. They take some paper and tape from Mom and Dad. They do not ask. They think it is a surprise.

They wrap their tower with the paper. They use a lot of tape. They make it very tight. They do not see their tower anymore. They only see paper.

They run to Mom and Dad. They say, "Look, look! We have a gift for Grandma too! It is our tower!"

Mom and Dad are surprised. They see the big paper ball. They do not see the tower. They are not happy. They say, "Oh, no! You took our paper and tape! You wrapped your tower! You ruined your tower and our paper!"

Ben and Mia are sad. They do not understand. They say, "But we wanted to make Grandma happy! We wanted to give her our tower!"

Mom and Dad sigh. They hug Ben and Mia. They say, "We know, we know. You are very sweet. But you should not take things without asking. And you should not wrap things that are not gifts. Your tower was beautiful. Grandma would have loved to see it. But now it is gone. Can you unwrap it?"

Ben and Mia nod. They try to unwrap their tower. But it is hard. The tape is very sticky. The paper is very tight. They need help. Mom and Dad help them. They unwrap their tower. They see the blocks again. They are happy.

Mom and Dad smile. They say, "Yes, it is. And we have an idea. Why don't we take a picture of your tower? Then we can send it to Grandma. She will see your tower and your smiles. She will be very happy."

Ben and Mia are happy. They say, "You're welcome, you're welcome! We love you, Grandma!"

They hug Mom and Dad. They hug each other. They play with their tower. They are careful. They do not wrap it again.

One day, Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They saw a big rat run out of a hole. Lily was scared and screamed. Tom was brave and chased the rat with a stick.

"Go away, rat! You are dirty and bad!" Tom shouted.

The rat was fast and clever. It dodged the stick and ran to the pond. It jumped into the water and swam away.

Lily and Tom followed the rat to the pond. They saw the rat wash itself in the water. It looked graceful and shiny. It had long whiskers and a curly tail.

"Wow, the rat is not so bad. It is pretty and clean!" Lily said.

Tom felt sorry for the rat. He threw the stick away and said, "You are right, Lily. The rat is not our enemy. It is just a different animal. Maybe it was looking for food or a friend."

The rat heard Tom and Lily. It peeked out of the water and squeaked. It seemed to say thank you and goodbye. Then it swam to the other side of the pond and disappeared.

Lily and Tom smiled and waved to the rat. They learned that not all rats are dirty and bad. Some rats are graceful and nice. They decided to play something else and leave the rat alone.

"Wow, look at this box!" Tom says. "It is so cool! Maybe there is something inside. Let's open it!"

Sam is scared. He does not like the symbol. He thinks it is bad. He says, "No, Tom, don't open it! The symbol is not cool. It is mean. It can hurt us. Let's go away!"

Tom does not listen. He wants to see what is in the box. He says, "Don't be silly, Sam. The symbol is just a picture. It can't hurt us. I want to open it. Come on, help me!"

Sam refuses. He shakes his head. He says, "No, Tom, I won't help you. I don't want to touch the box. I don't want to see what is in it. I want to go home. Bye, Tom!"

Sam runs away. He leaves Tom alone with the box. Tom is angry. He says, "Fine, Sam, go home! You are a chicken! I don't need you. I can open the box by myself!"

Tom pulls the box. He tries to open it. But the box is heavy. And the box is locked. Tom can't open it. He gets tired. He gets bored. He gets sad. He says, "Maybe Sam was right. Maybe the box is not cool. Maybe the box is mean. Maybe I should go home too."

Tom leaves the box. He runs after Sam. He says, "Sam, wait for me! I'm sorry, Sam. You are not a chicken. You are my friend. Can we play together again?"

Sam hears Tom. He stops. He turns around. He sees Tom. He smiles. He says, "Yes, Tom, you are my friend too. I'm sorry, too. I was scared. Can we play together again?"

Tom and Sam hug. They are happy. They forget about the box. They play with cars and blocks. They are friends. The end.

But then, they hear a voice. It is Mom. She says, "Boys, what are you doing? It is time for lunch. Come out of the tunnel, please."

Tom and Sam stop driving. They look at each other. They say, "Oh no, Mom found us. What do we do?"

They think for a moment. Then, they have an idea. They say, "Mom, we are not here. We are in the park. We are playing with the ducks. Quack quack!"

They hope Mom will believe them. They cover their mouths and giggle. They wait for Mom to go away.

But Mom is not fooled. She says, "Nice try, boys. But I can see your feet. They are sticking out of the blanket. They are wide and dirty. Come out of the tunnel, please. It is time for lunch. You can play again later."

Tom and Sam sigh. They know Mom is right. They come out of the tunnel. They say, "OK, Mom. We are sorry. We were just having fun. We are the drivers of the tunnel. Beep beep!"

Mom smiles. She says, "I know, boys. You are very creative. But you also need to eat and wash. Come on, let's go to the kitchen. You can tell me more about your tunnel later."

Tom and Sam nod. They follow Mom to the kitchen. They still hold their cars and trucks. They are happy. They are the drivers of the tunnel. Beep beep!

Mia liked to play with her kite. She had a kite with a long strip of cloth that moved in the wind. She ran with her kite in the park and watched it fly high in the sky. She felt happy and free.

One day, she saw a bird in a tree. The bird was big and had brown and white feathers. It looked at Mia and her kite with its bright eyes. Mia wanted to say hello to the bird. She stopped running and waved at it.

"Hi, bird! Do you like my kite?" Mia asked.

The bird did not answer. It flew out of the tree and towards Mia's kite. It grabbed the strip of cloth with its beak and pulled hard. Mia felt a tug on her hand. She tried to hold on to her kite, but the bird was stronger. It pulled the kite away from Mia and flew away with it.

"Hey, that's my kite! Give it back!" Mia shouted. She was sad and angry. She wanted her kite back.

She ran after the bird, but it was too fast. It flew over the roofs and out of sight. Mia stopped and cried. She had lost her kite.

A man saw Mia crying and came to help. He was wearing a blue hat and a green coat. He had a kind smile.

"What's wrong, little girl? Why are you crying?" he asked.

"A bird took my kite. It was a big bird with brown and white feathers. It flew away with my kite and I can't find it," Mia sobbed.

The man felt sorry for Mia. He had a kite in his bag. It was a kite with a star shape and a rainbow tail. He took it out and gave it to Mia.

"Here, you can have my kite. It's very pretty and colorful. Maybe it will make you feel better," he said.

Mia looked at the kite. It was different from her kite, but it was also very nice. She smiled and thanked the man.

"Thank you, mister. You are very kind. Can I fly your kite?" she asked.

"Of course, you can. Let me help you. Hold this string and run with me. When the wind is strong, release the string and let the kite fly," he said.

He held Mia's hand and ran with her. The wind blew and the kite lifted off the ground. It soared in the air, making a graceful arc. Mia watched it with wonder and joy. She forgot about her lost kite and the bird. She felt happy and free again.

The boy said, "I am sorry, sir, but I do not know you. I came here with my father. He is a carpenter and he came to fix your door. I stared at you because I think you are interesting. You have a big crown and a long robe. Why do you need them?"

The king was surprised by the boy's words. He felt ashamed of his pride and his harshness. He realized that he did not need to be so mean and bossy to be a good king. He needed to be kind and fair and humble. He said to the boy, "You are a smart and brave boy. You have taught me a lesson. I do not need these things to be a king. I need to be a good leader and a good friend. Will you forgive me and be my friend?"

The boy nodded and hugged the king. The king smiled and hugged him back. He decided to be a better king and a better person. He thanked the boy and his father and invited them to stay in the castle. He also treated his people with more respect and love. They were happy and grateful. They learned that staring can be a way of showing interest and not disrespect. They also learned that being obedient does not mean being afraid. It means being loyal and helpful. They all lived in peace and harmony.

Tom and Anna are playing in the kitchen. They see a big bag of potatoes on the floor. Tom has an idea.

"Let's make potato soup!" he says to Anna.

"OK!" Anna says. "How do we do that?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He remembers what his mom does when she makes soup. He takes a potato and a knife from the drawer.

"First, we need to cut the potatoes," he says. He tries to cut the potato, but it is too hard. He pushes harder, but the knife slips and cuts his finger. He drops the potato and the knife and cries.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" he screams.

Anna hears him and runs to him. She sees the blood on his finger and the mess on the floor.

"Tom, are you OK?" she asks. She hugs him and tries to calm him down.

"I'm sorry, Anna," Tom says. "I wanted to make soup, but I hurt myself."

Anna looks at the bag of potatoes. She has another idea.

"It's OK, Tom," she says. "We don't need to cut the potatoes. We can shake them!"

She takes a potato and shows him. She shakes it up and down, left and right, fast and slow. She makes funny noises as she does.

"Shake, shake, shake! Potato, potato, potato!" she says.

Tom stops crying and smiles. He takes another potato and joins her. They shake the potatoes and laugh.

"Shake, shake, shake! Potato, potato, potato!" they say.

They have fun shaking the potatoes, until they hear a voice.

"Tom! Anna! What are you doing?" It is their mom. She comes into the kitchen and sees the potatoes everywhere.

She is not happy. She looks at Tom's finger and the knife. She is worried.

"Tom, did you cut yourself?" she asks. She takes his hand and puts a band-aid on it.

"Yes, mom," Tom says. "I'm sorry, mom. We wanted to make soup, but we shook the potatoes instead."

Mom sighs. She is not angry, but she is not pleased.

"Tom, Anna, I appreciate your creativity, but this is not how you make soup. And this is not how you keep the kitchen tidy. You need to be careful with knives and clean up after yourselves. Do you understand?" she says.

Tom and Anna nod. They feel sorry for making a mess.

"We understand, mom," they say. "We're sorry, mom. Can we help you tidy up?"

Mom smiles. She is glad they are sorry and want to help.

"Of course you can, my loves," she says. "But first, let me make you some real potato soup. You must be hungry after all that shaking."

She takes the potatoes and the pot and goes to the stove. Tom and Anna follow her. They help her wash the potatoes and peel them. They watch her cut them and put them in the pot. They smell the soup as it cooks. They are hungry and excited.

"Mom, you make the best soup," they say.

Mom hugs them and kisses them.

"Thank you, my loves," she says. "And you make the best potato shakers."

Just then, a group of hunters came into the jungle. They wanted to catch Leo and take him away. Leo heard them coming and he started to roar loudly. The monkeys and the birds were scared, but the tortoise said, "Don't worry, I have a plan." 

The tortoise told the monkeys and the birds to make a lot of noise and distract the hunters. Amy and the cat became friends. They played on the carpet in the dark room every day. The cat would shrug, and Amy would laugh. They were happy and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Amy went to the doctor with her mom. Amy was feeling terrible. She had a big pain in her arm. The doctor looked at Amy's arm and said, "We need to take an x-ray to see what's wrong."

Amy was scared, but her mom held her hand. The doctor took the x-ray and showed it to Amy and her mom. There was a crack in her arm. The doctor said, "You have a broken arm. I will put a cast on it, and it will get better soon."

Amy felt better with the cast on her arm. When she got home, her brother wanted to play. He tried to grab her arm, but Amy said, "No, don't touch my arm! It hurts!" Her brother said sorry and gave her a hug. They played a different game, and Amy was happy.

In the end, the bear won the race. But the bee and the ant became good friends. They learned that helping others is better than winning alone. And that was the best prize of all.

Tim and Mia are playing with their toy cars in the garden. They like to zoom them on the grass and make noises. Mia has a red car and Tim has a blue car. They pretend they are racing each other.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Mia says. "My car is faster than yours!"

"No, it's not!" Tim says. "My car has a tail. It makes it go faster. See?" He shows Mia the tail of his car. It is a piece of string tied to the back.

Mia laughs. "That's not a tail. That's a string. It doesn't make your car faster. It makes it slower. Watch!" She pulls the string and the car stops.

"Hey, stop that!" Tim says. "You broke my car!"

"I did not!" Mia says. "It was already broken. The string is not part of the car. It's just a string."

"Yes, it is!" Tim says. "It's my car's tail. It's special. You broke it!"

They start to argue. They forget to play with their cars. They are not having fun.

Mom hears them and comes to the garden. She sees the cars and the string. She sees Tim and Mia looking angry.

"What's going on here?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"

"Mia broke my car!" Tim says.

"No, I didn't!" Mia says.

Mom picks up the cars and the string. She looks at them.

"These are nice cars," Mom says. "But they don't need a string to zoom. The string is not a tail. It's just a string. You can use it for something else. Like a kite. Or a necklace. Or a snake. Do you want to try?"

Tim and Mia look at each other. They think about it. They nod.

"OK," they say.

Mom helps them untie the string. She gives them each a piece. She shows them how to make a kite, a necklace, and a snake. They have fun. They forget to fight. They zoom their cars again. They share their string toys. They are happy.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. They want to try it.

"Come on, Mia, let's go to the slide!" Tom says.

Mia looks at the slide. It is very high and long. It has a tunnel in the middle. The tunnel is dark.

"I don't know, Tom. It looks scary," Mia says.

"Don't be afraid, Mia. It will be fun. I will go first, and then you can follow me," Tom says.

He runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. He seats on the top and smiles at Mia.

"See, Mia, it's easy. Now you come too," he says.

Mia walks slowly to the slide. She climbs up the ladder. She seats next to Tom. She feels anxious. She does not like the dark tunnel.

"Tom, I don't want to go. Can we go back?" she says.

"No, Mia, you can do it. Just close your eyes and slide down. I will wait for you at the bottom," he says.

He pushes himself and slides down. He shouts with joy.

"Wow, that was awesome! Come on, Mia, your turn!" he says.

Mia hears Tom's voice. She wants to be brave like him. She closes her eyes and slides down. She feels the wind in her hair. She feels the tunnel around her. She feels the sun on her face. She opens her eyes and sees Tom.

She did it! She slides down the slide!

She smiles at Tom. He smiles back.

"That was fun, Tom! Thank you for helping me," she says.

"You're welcome, Mia. You are very brave. Do you want to go again?" he says.

"Yes, Tom, let's go again!" she says.

They run to the slide and climb up the ladder. They seat on the top and slide down. They laugh and have fun. They are not afraid of the dark anymore. They are happy.

Sara and Tom were very excited to see the parade. They wore their colorful hats and waved their flags. They followed their mom and dad to the big street where the parade would pass by.

"Look, Sara, there are the clowns!" Tom said, pointing at the funny people with big noses and shoes. "They make me laugh!"

"And there are the dancers!" Sara said, admiring the pretty people with shiny dresses and feathers. "They move so well!"

They watched the parade with joy, clapping and cheering for every group that passed by. They saw the animals, the cars, the bands, and the balloons. They were having so much fun!

But then, something strange happened. One of the balloons, a big red one, popped loudly. Sara and Tom were scared and covered their ears. They saw the balloon fall to the ground, and reveal something inside.

"What is that?" Sara asked, curious.

"It's a present!" Tom said, happy. "Someone hid a present inside the balloon!"

They ran to the balloon, hoping to get the present. But when they got there, they saw that the present was not for them. It had a tag that said "To Mia, from Grandma and Grandpa. Happy birthday!"

Sara and Tom felt sad and disappointed. They wanted the present so badly. They looked at each other, and thought about taking it.

But then, they remembered what their mom and dad had taught them. They knew that taking something that was not theirs was wrong. They knew that Mia would be very happy to get the present from her grandparents. They knew that they should be kind and honest.

They decided to leave the present where it was, and wait for Mia to find it. They went back to their mom and dad, and told them what they had seen.

"Good job, Sara and Tom!" their mom and dad said, proud. "You did the right thing. You are very good children!"

Sara and Tom felt happy and proud, too. They learned that being good was better than having a present. They hugged their mom and dad, and watched the rest of the parade. They enjoyed the colorful and fun show, and forgot about the present. They had a wonderful day!

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big lawn with many flowers and toys. They also had a dog named Spot who was very friendly and loved to run and jump.

One day, Anna and Ben saw a new family moving in next door. They had a fancy car and a fancy house. They also had a cat named Fluffy who was very fluffy and had a shiny collar. Anna and Ben wanted to say hello and play with Fluffy, but their mom told them to wait until the new family was settled.

The next day, Anna and Ben went to the fence and called Fluffy. Fluffy came to the fence and looked at them with her green eyes. She seemed nice and curious. Anna and Ben reached out their hands to pet her, but Fluffy hissed and scratched them. Anna and Ben cried and ran back to their mom. Their mom put some cream on their scratches and hugged them.

"Why did Fluffy hurt us?" Anna asked. "We just wanted to be friends."

"Maybe Fluffy is scared of new people and dogs," their mom said. "Maybe she needs some time to get used to us. Or maybe she is just not a nice cat. Some cats are like that."

Anna and Ben felt sad and angry. They did not like Fluffy anymore. They wanted to make her suffer. They thought of ways to scare her or hurt her. They thought of throwing rocks at her, or spraying her with water, or letting Spot chase her.

But then they remembered what their mom always told them. "Do not do to others what you do not want them to do to you. Be kind and gentle to all living things. They have feelings too."

Anna and Ben looked at each other and felt ashamed. They knew their mom was right. They did not want Fluffy to suffer. They wanted to be good and nice. They decided to leave Fluffy alone and hope that she would be nicer someday. They went to play with Spot and their toys. They had fun and forgot about Fluffy.

The moral of the story is: Do not be mean to others, even if they are mean to you. Be kind and gentle to all living things. They have feelings too.

Ben was a mailman. He liked to deliver letters to people. He had a big bag of letters and a blue bike. He rode his bike from house to house and put letters in the mailboxes.

One day, it was very gloomy. The sky was gray and it was raining. Ben put on his yellow raincoat and his hat. He still wanted to deliver letters, but he was not happy. He wished the sun would come out.

He came to a house with a red door. He took out a letter and walked to the mailbox. But before he could put the letter in, a big dog came out of the house. The dog was barking and growling. It ran towards Ben.

Sam and his puppy find a big field. The field has grass and a ball. Sam and his puppy want to play with the ball. Sam throws the ball and his puppy runs after it. His puppy catches the ball and brings it back to Sam. They do this many times. They have fun.

Sam and his puppy get tired. They sit on the grass and drink some water. They cuddle and rest. They are happy. They love each other. They love their walk.

Tom and Lily were playing on the beach. They liked to look at the fish and the shells in the water. They saw a big boat with many people on it. The boat stopped near a reef.

"Look, Lily, the boat is going to the reef. Maybe they want to see the fish too," Tom said.

"Can we go to the reef, Tom? I want to see the fish too," Lily said.

Tom shook his head. "No, Lily, the reef is too far and too deep. We have to stay on the beach. But we can whistle to the fish. Maybe they will come to us."

Tom and Lily put their lips together and blew. They made a whistling sound. They hoped the fish would hear them and swim to them.

They whistled and whistled. Then they saw something in the water. It was a big, purple fish. It had a long, pointy nose and a stripe on its side. It was a swordfish.

The swordfish heard the whistling and was curious. It swam closer to the beach. It saw Tom and Lily and waved its nose at them.

"Wow, Lily, look at that fish. It is so big and purple. And it has a sword on its nose. Do you think it is friendly?" Tom said.

"I don't know, Tom. It looks scary. Maybe we should stop whistling. Maybe it will go away," Lily said.

But the swordfish did not go away. It liked the whistling. It wanted to play with Tom and Lily. It jumped out of the water and made a splash.

Tom and Lily were surprised and scared. They ran away from the water. They hid behind a rock.

The swordfish was sad. It did not mean to scare Tom and Lily. It wanted to be their friend. It whistled back to them. It hoped they would come back.

But Tom and Lily did not come back. They stayed behind the rock. They waited for the boat to leave. They hoped the swordfish would leave too. They did not want to play with the swordfish. They thought it was too big and too purple and too scary.

Anna lived in a small village with her mama and papa. She liked to play with her friends, sing songs, and pick flowers. She was a happy girl.

One day, a big storm came to the village. It made loud noises and scary flashes. It broke some houses and trees. Anna was very afraid. She ran to her mama and papa and hugged them tight. They hugged her back and told her it was okay.

The next day, the storm was gone. But the village was very sad. Some people had no homes. Some people had no food. Some people had no clothes. Anna wanted to help them. She asked her mama and papa what she could do.

They said she could share her toys, her books, and her snacks with the people who had none. They said she could sing songs, tell jokes, and make drawings to make them smile. They said she could hug them and say nice words to make them feel better.

Anna did all these things. She gave her teddy bear to a little boy who had lost his. She read her favorite story to a little girl who had no books. She shared her cookies with an old man who had no food. She sang a song, told a joke, and made a drawing for a lady who had no clothes. She hugged them all and said, "I am your friend. I care about you. You are not alone."

The people in the village were very grateful. They thanked Anna and hugged her back. They said, "You are a kind girl. You have a big heart. You make us happy."

Anna felt happy too. She learned that hugs can help heal sad hearts. She learned that she could make a difference in her village. She learned that she was not afraid of storms anymore. She learned that she was brave.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to look for insects in the grass and the flowers. They saw ants, bees, and butterflies. Sara wanted to find a ladybug, because they were red and pretty.

"Look, Ben, a ladybug!" Sara said, pointing to a leaf. She ran to catch it, but Ben stopped her.

"No, Sara, don't touch it!" Ben said. "Ladybugs can bite!"

Sara was scared. She did not want to be bitten by a ladybug. She backed away from the leaf.

"Are you sure, Ben?" Sara asked. "How do you know?"

Ben nodded. He said he learned it from a book. He said ladybugs were not really bugs, but beetles. He said beetles had hard shells and strong jaws. He said some beetles could order other insects for lunch.

Sara gasped. She did not want to be lunch for a beetle. She decided to leave the ladybug alone. She said she was sorry for trying to catch it.

Ben smiled. He said it was okay. He said ladybugs were not mean, but they could defend themselves. He said ladybugs were good for plants, because they ate bad insects that hurt the flowers.

Sara and Ben agreed that ladybugs were cool, but they did not want to touch them. They went to look for other insects that were safer and softer. They had fun in the park.
