One day, their mom said, "Ben and Lily, you have to organize your toys. If you don't, I will give them away to other kids who need them."

Ben and Lily did not want to lose their toys, so they said, "Okay, mom, we will organize them." But they did not really mean it. They just put some toys in a big box and hid it under the bed. They thought mom would not see it.

But mom was not fooled. She looked under the bed and saw the box. She opened it and saw a terrible mess. There were cars, dolls, books, crayons, and even socks in the box. The socks were dirty and smelly, and they did not match.

"Ben and Lily, what is this?" mom asked. "This is not organizing. This is a terrible way to treat your toys and your socks. You have to sort them and put them in the right places. And you have to wash your socks. They are very stinky."

Ben and Lily felt ashamed. They knew they had been lazy and naughty. They said, "Sorry, mom. We will do better. We will organize our toys and our socks. And we will wash our socks. Please don't give them away."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Ben and Lily. I'm glad you understand. I love you and I want you to take care of your things. Now, let's go and organize together."

"Stop, Ben!" Lily said. "That is mean. The ducks and fish are hungry and peaceful. They do not like stones."

"I do not care," Ben said. "It is fun. Watch this!" He threw a big stone at a duck. The duck quacked and flew away.

Lily felt an urge to cry. She loved animals and did not want them to be hurt. She ran to the pond and picked up some bread. She threw it to the fish and the other ducks. They came closer and ate the bread. They looked happy and peaceful.

Suddenly, a big splash appeared in the pond. Lily and Ben saw a frog jump out of the water. It landed on a lily pad and croaked. It was green and shiny. It had big eyes and a long tongue.

"Wow!" Lily and Ben said. "A frog!"

They forgot their fight and ran to the pond. They wanted to see the frog better. They were careful not to scare it. They smiled and laughed. The frog smiled and croaked. They became friends.

Anna and Ben were playing with clay. They liked to make different shapes and feel the texture of the clay. It was soft and squishy in their hands. They made balls, snakes, stars and flowers.

"Look, I made a wise owl!" Anna said, showing Ben her clay owl. She had used a stick to make eyes and a beak. "It can see everything and knows many things."

"That's nice, Anna. But I made a magic rabbit!" Ben said, showing Anna his clay rabbit. He had used a leaf to make ears and a carrot to make a nose. "It can hop very fast and disappear when it wants to."

"Wow, Ben. That's cool. Can you make it disappear?" Anna asked, curious.

"Sure, watch this!" Ben said, holding his clay rabbit in his hand. He closed his eyes and said a magic word. Then he opened his hand and showed Anna. The clay rabbit was gone!

"Where did it go?" Anna asked, amazed.

"I don't know. Maybe it hopped away to another place. Or maybe it is hiding somewhere. It is a magic rabbit, after all." Ben said, shrugging.

"Can you make it come back?" Anna asked, hoping.

"Maybe. Let me try." Ben said, closing his eyes again and saying another magic word. Then he opened his hand and showed Anna. The clay rabbit was back!

"Wow, Ben. You are very good at magic. How did you do that?" Anna asked, impressed.

"It's a secret. But I can tell you. I have another clay rabbit in my pocket. I just switched them when you were not looking." Ben said, whispering.

"That's not magic. That's cheating!" Anna said, frowning.

"No, it's not. It's a trick. And tricks are fun. Do you want to learn how to do it?" Ben asked, smiling.

"Okay. But only if you teach me how to make a wise owl too." Anna said, nodding.

"Deal. Come on, let's play some more." Ben said, taking Anna's hand.

They played with clay for a long time, making more shapes and feeling the texture of the clay. They also learned how to do tricks and make each other laugh. They had a lot of fun.

"No, wait!" said Tara. "It might be dangerous. We should warn the others."

But Tom did not listen. He swam faster and faster towards the yellow thing. Tara followed him and tried to stop him.

"Tom, come back!" she shouted. "It's not a ball, it's a balloon! And the tail is a rope! It can hurt you!"

"Ow, ow, ow!" he wailed. "It hurts, it hurts!"

Tara swam to him and hugged him. She was scared and sorry for him.

"I'm sorry, Tom," she said. "I tried to warn you. Are you okay?"

Tom nodded, but he still felt sore. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be careful and listen to his friends. He learned that some unusual things are not good to play with. He learned to love his reef and his home.

Dan is a bald man. He likes to play with matches. He thinks they are fun and bright. But matches are not toys. They can make fire and hurt people.

One day, Dan finds a box of matches in his kitchen. He is very happy. He wants to see the matches light up. He takes one match and moves it to the stove. He turns on the stove and puts the match near the flame.

"Whoosh!" The match catches fire. Dan is scared. He drops the match on the floor. The floor has a rug. The rug starts to burn.

"Help! Help!" Dan shouts. He runs to the door. He wants to get out.

But his mom is there. She hears Dan and smells the smoke. She is very angry and worried. She grabs a bucket of water and throws it on the fire. She puts out the fire.

"Dan, what did you do?" she asks. "Why did you play with matches? You could have burned the house and yourself!"

"I'm sorry, Mom," Dan says. "I didn't know matches were bad. I just wanted to see them."

Lily and Ben are not afraid. They go to the dog and stroke its fur. The dog wags its tail and licks their faces. It is very friendly and cute. Lily and Ben giggle and hug the dog. They do not notice the red spots on its skin.

The next day, Lily and Ben wake up with an itch. They scratch their arms, their legs and their faces. They have red spots all over. They feel hot and sore. They cry and call their moms.

Their moms come and look at them. They are worried and angry. They ask them what happened. Lily and Ben tell them about the dog in the park. They say they did not know it had an itch. They say they are sorry.

Their moms hug them and say it is okay. They say they have to go to the doctor. They say the doctor will give them some medicine and some cream. They say they will be better soon. They say they have to be more careful next time. They say they still love them.

Lily and Ben nod and say they love them too. They say they love the dog too, but they will not pet it again. They say they hope the dog will be better too. They say they still have each other. They are reliable friends.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they decided to be sailors and sail on a big boat. They put on their hats and scarves and took a big cardboard box to the backyard.

"Ahoy, matey!" Max said to Lily. "Are you ready to sail the seven seas?"

"Aye, aye, captain!" Lily said. "But where is our boat?"

Max pointed to the box. "This is our boat, silly. We just have to use our imagination."

They climbed into the box and pretended to steer and row. They sang songs and told stories. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Max got too excited and started to jump and rock the box. He was clumsy and knocked over Lily's hat and scarf.

"Hey, stop that!" Lily said. "You are making a mess. You have to behave, or we will sink."

Max did not listen. He kept jumping and rocking. He was having too much fun.

But then, the box tipped over and they both fell out. They landed on the grass and got dirty.

"Oops!" Max said. "Sorry, Lily. I did not mean to do that."

Lily was not happy. She was wet and cold and her hat and scarf were gone.

"That's not how sailors play, Max. You are a bad sailor. You are not my matey anymore."

She got up and ran to the house. She left Max alone in the backyard.

Max felt sad. He did not want to make Lily mad. He wanted to be her matey again.

He looked around and saw her hat and scarf on the ground. He picked them up and ran after her.

"Lily, wait!" he said. "I'm sorry. I was clumsy. I will behave. Please be my matey again."

He gave her the hat and scarf and hugged her.

Lily looked at him and smiled. She hugged him back.

"It's okay, Max. I forgive you. You are a good sailor. You are my matey again."

They went back to the box and played some more. They were careful and gentle. They had a lot of fun.

Ben and Jen had nowhere to go. They looked for another shelter, but they could not find any. They looked for a way out, but they could not find any. They were trapped and alone. The cat was getting closer and closer. He opened his mouth and showed his sharp teeth. He was ready to eat them.

Ben and Jen wished they had a better shelter, or a bigger supply of food and water, or an easy way to escape. But they had none of those things. They only had each other. They hugged and said goodbye. The cat pounced and caught them. He ate them and licked his paws. He was happy and had everything he wanted.

Lila was a brilliant girl who loved to learn new things. She liked to read books, play games, and ask questions. She also liked to help her dad, who was a scientist. He worked in a big place with many cells. Cells are very small things that make up all living things.

One day, Lila's dad let her come with him to his work. He showed her his lab, where he had many machines and tools. He also showed her his microscope, which could make the cells look bigger. Lila was amazed by the different shapes and colors of the cells. She wanted to see more.

Lila's dad had to go to a meeting, so he told Lila to stay in his office and play with his books and toys. He said he would be back soon. Lila nodded and said okay. But she was very curious about the cells. She wondered what they would look like if she mixed them together.

She sneaked out of the office and went back to the lab. She found some tubes with different cells in them. She took a few and poured them into a big bowl. She stirred them with a spoon and watched them swirl. She thought they looked pretty.

But then, something happened. The cells started to grow and change. They became bigger and bigger, and they made strange noises. They also started to move and jump out of the bowl. Lila was scared. She ran out of the lab and looked for her dad.

She found him in the hallway, talking to some other people. She ran to him and hugged him. She told him what she did and how sorry she was. She said she wanted to see the cells, but she didn't know they would do that.

Lila's dad was surprised and worried. He told the other people to go to the lab and check on the cells. He also told Lila that he was not angry, but that she should never do that again. He said that cells are very important and delicate, and that they need to be handled with care. He said that he was glad that she was safe and that he loved her.

Lila felt relieved and happy. She said that she loved him too and that she learned her lesson. She said that she still wanted to learn more about cells, but only with his help. He smiled and said that he was proud of her and that he would teach her more. He took her hand and they went back to his office. They played with his books and toys until it was time to go home.

He got up and looked out the window. He saw more leaves like that, falling from the trees. They were all different colors and shapes. Some were round, some were long, some were spiky, some were smooth. Tom wondered why the leaves were so unusual.

He ran outside to catch some leaves. He wanted to show them to his mom and dad. He saw other kids playing with the leaves, too. They made piles, and hats, and boats, and animals. They had fun with the unusual leaves.

Tom's mom and dad came out and saw him. They smiled and hugged him. They told him that the leaves were unusual because it was autumn. Autumn was a time when the leaves changed and fell. They said it was a beautiful and special time of the year.

Tom was happy. He liked autumn and the unusual leaves. He thanked the leaf that woke him up. He said it was a good leaf. He put it in his pocket and went inside with his mom and dad. He wanted to keep the leaf and remember his dream.

Finally, she reached home. She dropped the weight on the floor, feeling exhausted. She tried to rest, but the weight was pressing down on her body, making it hard to breathe. 

Her mom came in and saw her. "Tina, what is that weight? Why did you bring it home?"

Tina tried to explain, but her mom was angry. She took the weight away and told Tina never to carry something so heavy again. 

Tina was sad and tired. She lay down to rest, but the weight had made her too exhausted and she couldn't sleep.

The End.

Lily was a dog who loved to chew bones. She had a big bone that she found in the park. She hid it under her bed and chewed it every day. She did not allow anyone to touch her bone. It was hers and hers alone.

One day, Lily heard a knock on the door. It was her friend Max, another dog who lived next door. Max wanted to play with Lily. He wagged his tail and barked.

"Hi, Lily! Do you want to play with me? We can run and chase and fetch and roll!"

Lily looked at her bone. She wanted to play with Max, but she did not want to leave her bone. She was afraid someone might take it. She barked back.

"Hi, Max! I want to play with you, but I have something very important under my bed. It is my bone. It is big and tasty and mine. You can not have it. You can not touch it. You can not see it."

Max was curious. He wanted to see Lily's bone. He thought maybe they could share it. He sniffed and sneaked towards Lily's bed. He tried to peek under it.

Lily saw what Max was doing. She growled and ran to her bed. She blocked Max with her body. She showed her teeth and barked.

"Go away, Max! This is my bone! You can not have it! You can not touch it! You can not see it!"

Max was scared. He did not like Lily's growl and teeth. He backed away and whimpered.

"Sorry, Lily. I did not mean to make you angry. I just wanted to play with you. And see your bone. Maybe it is nice. Maybe we can be friends."

Lily felt bad. She did not want to make Max scared. She did not want to lose her friend. She looked at her bone. She looked at Max. She had an idea. She wagged her tail and barked.

"OK, Max. I am sorry too. I was too mean. You can see my bone. But you can not have it. You can not touch it. You can only look. And then we can play. OK?"

Max nodded and smiled. He was happy. He followed Lily to her bed. He looked at her bone. It was big and tasty. He licked his lips. But he did not touch it. He respected Lily's rule. He was a good friend.

Lily was proud. She showed Max her bone. She shared her secret. She was a good friend too.

They looked at the bone for a while. Then they left it under the bed. They went outside and played. They ran and chased and fetched and rolled. They had fun. They were calm and happy. They were friends.

But then, Bongo saw a lion coming towards him. He was scared and didn't know what to do. He tried to run away, but his foot got caught on a branch. The lion was getting closer and closer. Bongo closed his eyes and wished he could stretch his arms and fly away.

Suddenly, Bongo heard a loud roar. It was his mommy and daddy! They had come to rescue him. They scared the lion away and brought Bongo back home safely. Bongo learned that it's important to listen to his mommy and daddy and not go on adventures alone.

Timmy said, "Mommy, look at the big bird! Can we go see it?" 

His mom said, "Sure, but we have to be careful. Ostriches can be dangerous." 

They walked over to the ostrich and Timmy said, "Hello, Mr. Ostrich! You are very big!" 

The ostrich didn't say anything back and started to walk away. Timmy got sad and said, "Mommy, why did the ostrich leave? Did I do something wrong?" 

His mom said, "No, Timmy. Sometimes animals just want to be alone. Let's go play on the swings instead." 

Timmy smiled and they went to play on the swings. Even though they didn't get to talk to the ostrich, they still had a fun day at the park.

The boy went to his mom and asked what happened. "I'm afraid it's rotted," she said softly.

The boy was really mad. He had worked so hard on his stitch and now it was gone forever. He got so angry he even cried.

But in the end, his mom hugged him and said, "It's okay. We can make a new stitch together so it will be just like the first one."

So, the boy and his mom worked together to make a new stitch which was even more beautiful than the first. The boy was so happy, and from then on, he made sure to keep his stitch safe from the elements.

Once upon a time there were two little birds, Peter and Lucy. Peter was a bright and helpful bird, while Lucy was a bossy bird.

One day, Lucy asked Peter to help her gather some prunes from a nearby tree. Peter was glad to help, so he flew up to the tree and started to act. He opened his wings and flapped them very fast, so that he could reach the prunes.

However, Lucy was impatient and bossy. She started to tell Peter what to do and shouted at him. She yelled, "Go faster! Faster!"

Peter became scared and flew away.

The moral of the story is that it is important to be patient and kind when helping others. If you are bossy, people may not be so willing to help you.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jerry. Jerry was feeling a bit miserable, so he decided to take a little trip in a jet. 

He was flying along in his jet when suddenly, he started to sneeze! Jerry was feeling so sick that he had to turn back and go home. 

When he got home, his mother asked him why he was back so soon. Jerry told her he had to come home because he was feeling too sick to continue his trip. 

His mother said, "Jerry, it's very important to take care of your health. If you don't feel well, you should never try to push yourself too hard. You should always make sure you take good care of your body, and then you can do anything you want to do."

Jerry thanked his mother for the advice and said he would always remember her words. From then on, Jerry always made sure to take care of himself whenever he didn't feel well. 

Moral of the story: Take good care of your health, so you can do the things you want to do.

Lucy was so happy and thankful to her lucky towel. She promised to always behave well so that her magical towel would always make rainbows and flowers when she waved it around.

Dolly and Lily played together. They swam and jumped in the water. Lily would wave to Dolly, and Dolly would wave back with her fin. They had lots of fun and became best friends. Every day, Lily would come to the sea to play with her unique dolphin friend, Dolly.

Bop stopped jumping and looked at Pip. He said, "Thank you for your opinion, Pip. I will be more careful." Bop and Pip played together all day, and they had lots of fun. Bop was happy that Pip cared about him, and he made sure to be safe while playing.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very stubborn. He wanted to do everything by himself. One day, Tim saw his dad's belt on the floor. He wanted to wear it, but it was too big for him.

Tim's mom saw him trying to wear the belt. She said, "Tim, that belt is too big for you. Let me help you." But Tim said, "No, I want to do it by myself!" Tim tried and tried, but he couldn't put on the belt.

Then, Tim's mom had an idea. She said, "Let's test something." She took a smaller belt and showed it to Tim. "Try this one," she said. Tim put on the smaller belt, and it fit him perfectly. Tim was very happy, and he learned that sometimes it's okay to ask for help.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Bobby. Bobby was very obedient. He always listened to his owner, Sam. One day, Sam said, "Bobby, I have a letter to send. Take it to the post for me."

Bobby took the letter in his mouth and went to the post. On his way, he saw a little girl who was weeping. She had lost her toy. Bobby went to her and said, "Don't weep. I will help you find your toy."

Bobby and the little girl looked everywhere for the toy. They found it under a big tree. The girl was happy and said, "Thank you, Bobby. You are a good dog." Bobby wagged his tail and went back to his job. He took the letter to the post.

When Bobby went back home, Sam was so proud of him. He gave Bobby a big treat for being such an obedient dog. The moral of the story is: always help others, and good things will come to you.

The cold wind stayed and everyone was still unhappy. Tim and Sam learned that they should be careful with mysterious things.

Tim saw his ball across the road and wanted to get it. He knew the road was dangerous, but he didn't want to lose his ball. As he was about to cross, a big, harsh dog barked at him. "Woof, woof!" said the dog. "Don't cross the road alone! It's not safe!"

Tim was scared, but he knew the dog was right. He ran to find his mom and told her what happened. "Mom, my ball is across the road, and a dog told me not to cross alone," Tim said. His mom held his hand and helped him cross the road safely. They saved the ball together.

From that day on, Tim always remembered to be careful near roads and to ask for help when he needed it. The big, harsh dog became his friend, and they played with the red ball together every day. Tim learned that it was important to listen to others and stay safe.

Sam looked everywhere for a rock to match his rare, shiny rock. He looked in his room, in the yard, and even at the park. But he couldn't find a match. Sam felt sad.

Then, Sam's mom gave him an idea. She said, "Why don't you use ice to match your rare, shiny rock?" Sam thought this was a great idea. He went to the freezer and took out a piece of ice. The ice was shiny, just like his rock. Sam was happy because he found a match for his rare, shiny rock. But soon, the ice started to melt. Sam felt sad again.

Sam's mom saw him and said, "Don't worry, Sam. You can always get more ice from the freezer to match your rock." Sam smiled and knew that he could always find a match for his rare, shiny rock with ice. And he lived happily ever after.

Lisa nods. She knows mom is right. She wants to be a good girl. She chews and chews and tries to blow a bubble. She pushes the gum with her tongue and makes a small pop.

"Look, mom, I did it!" Lisa says. She is proud of herself.

"Good job, Lisa!" mom says. She smiles and hugs her. "You are learning how to blow bubbles. That's fun. But remember, gum is delicate. It can break or stick. So be careful where you put it."

Lisa hugs mom back. She loves mom and gum. She thinks she is lucky. She chews and chews and tries to blow another bubble. She pushes the gum with her tongue and makes a bigger pop. She is happy and sweet.

As the night got colder, Max realized he should have listened to his owner. He curled up in a ball, using his tail to keep warm. But it wasn't enough, and Max got very sick. 

The next day, Max's owner found him lying outside and rushed him to the vet. But it was too late, and Max passed away. His owner was heartbroken and wished Max had listened and come inside when he was told.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her hose. One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Max. Lily felt anxious to talk to him, but she wanted to be friends.

"Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me and my hose?" asked Lily.

Max smiled and said, "Yes, please. That sounds like fun."

Lily welcomed Max to play with her. They had a great time spraying water all over the yard. But then, Max accidentally stepped on the hose and broke it. Water went everywhere and Lily's mom got mad.

Lily felt sad that her hose was broken and that Max had to go home. She wished they could have played longer.

"What happened, Timmy?" his mom asked.

"These chips are too spicy," Timmy said, still crying.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat melon. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big, juicy melon to eat. But Timmy accidentally dropped the melon on the ground and it got dirty.

Timmy was happy again and took a big bite of the melon. But he didn't like the taste. So, he asked his mom to release the seeds from the melon. His mom cut the melon open and released all the seeds. Timmy was happy again because he could eat the melon without the seeds. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cauliflower, but her mom always cooked too much. One day, Lily asked her mom why she cooked so much cauliflower. Her mom replied, "I want to make sure you have enough to eat."

Lily thought about it and said, "But mom, I can only eat a little bit. The rest goes to waste and our fridge is always empty."

Her mom realized Lily was right and said, "You're so smart, Lily. From now on, I'll only cook enough for us to eat. We don't want to waste food."

Lily felt happy that she could help her mom and they both enjoyed their delicious meal together. The moral of the story is that we should only take what we need and not waste things.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Piper. She was never afraid to try something new.

One day, Piper was walking through a forest. Her mum had urged her to keep away from the dirt path, but Piper didn't listen. As she walked down the path, she noticed a big, wide clearing.

She started walking towards it, when suddenly she heard a loud growling noise. Piper froze. She felt a wave of fear rush through her body. Looking around she noticed a big, dirty bear.

The bear walked up to Piper. "What are you doing in my clearing?," it asked. Piper could feel her body urge her to run, but she stayed put.

Piper swallowed then bravely replied, "I wanted to explore this place. I'm sorry if I disturbed you."

The bear listened to her and then smiled. "Well, I suppose I can let you stay," it said.

So, Piper and the bear became friends. They talked, laughed and explored the wide clearing together.

The hunter kept walking and saw a turtle. "Hello, turtle," said the hunter. "Do you know where I can find a big animal to catch?" The turtle looked at the hunter and said, "I am slow like you, but I know that if you keep looking, you will find what you want." The hunter thanked the turtle and walked on.

At last, the hunter found a big animal. He was so happy! The slow hunter took the big animal home to share with his family. They all ate and were full, and the hunter knew that being slow was not so bad after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky was very bored because he didn't have anything to do. He waddled around the pond, but it was all the same. He wanted something new to do.

One day, he met a frog named Freddy. "Hi Ducky," said Freddy. "What's up?"

"I'm bored," replied Ducky. "There's nothing to do around here."

"Well, I can show you something cool," said Freddy. "There's a swamp nearby. It's full of interesting things."

"Really?" asked Ducky, excitedly. "Can we go there?"

"Sure," said Freddy. "Follow me!"

So, Ducky followed Freddy to the swamp. It was a bit scary at first, but then Ducky saw all the different plants and animals living there. He was amazed! "This is so cool!" he quacked.

"I told you it was interesting," said Freddy. "I'm glad I could show you something new."

Ducky was grateful to Freddy for showing him the swamp. From that day on, he wasn't bored anymore. He had a new place to explore and new friends to meet.

The firemen are brave and strong. They spray water on the fire. They make the fire smaller and smaller. They stop the spark and the smoke. They are good.

Tom and Sue clap their hands. They cheer for the firemen. The firemen smile and wave. They are happy.

The firemen tell Tom and Sue to go back to the park. They say the fire is dangerous and dirty. They say the fire can hurt them and make them sick. They say they should stay away from the fire.

Tom and Sue nod their heads. They say thank you to the firemen. They run and run and spring down the hill. They go back to the park. They play with their ball and their bike. They are safe.

I want to finish my picture." Her mom said, "No, Sara, you have to help me now. The laundry is very full and we need to wash it. You can paint later."

Sara was sad. She put her paints away and went to her room. She saw her brother Ben playing with his cars on the floor. He had many cars of different sizes and colors. He made noises and pretended they were racing. Sara was envious. She said, "Ben, can I play with your cars too?" Ben said, "No, Sara, these are my cars. You have your paints. Go and paint something." He did not look at her.

Sara felt angry. She said, "But I can't paint now. Mom said I have to do the laundry. You don't have to do anything. That's not fair." Ben said, "Too bad. I don't care. Go away." He turned his back to her.

Sara did not go away. She had an idea. She took one of her paints and a brush and sneaked behind Ben. She painted a big red spot on his shirt. Ben did not notice. Sara smiled. She said, "There. Now you have to do the laundry too." She ran away.

Ben felt something wet on his back. He looked at his shirt and saw the red spot. He was shocked. He said, "Hey, what did you do? You ruined my shirt. Mom, Sara painted on my shirt. She's mean." He started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and came to the room. She saw the red spot on Ben's shirt and the paint on Sara's hand. She was angry. She said, "Sara, why did you do that? That was very naughty. You have to say sorry to Ben and help me with the laundry. And no more painting for today. You are in trouble."

Sara felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was envious of your cars. I wanted to play with them. I didn't mean to ruin your shirt." Ben said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I was mean to you. I should have shared my cars with you. You can play with them later." They hugged.

She hoped she would not be envious again. She hoped she would be good.

Tom and Lily were playing in the woods. They liked to pretend they were animals. Tom was a bear and Lily was a rabbit. They ran and hid and chased each other.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a hunter. He had a big gun and a mean dog. He wanted to catch the animals in the woods. He saw Tom and Lily and thought they were real animals. He aimed his gun at them.

"Run, Lily, run!" Tom shouted. He tried to scare the hunter away. He roared like a bear and threw sticks and stones. But the hunter did not go away. He laughed and shot his gun. Tom felt a pain in his leg. He fell down and cried.

Lily was scared. She wanted to help Tom. She saw a hole in the ground. It was a fox's den. She ran inside and called for the fox.

"Please, Mr. Fox, please help us!" she said. "The hunter is bad. He hurt Tom. He wants to hurt you too."

The fox was surprised. He did not like hunters. He did not like rabbits either. But he saw that Lily was brave and kind. He decided to be helpful.

"OK, little rabbit, I will help you," he said. "But you have to be quiet and do what I say."

The fox came out of his den. He saw the hunter and his dog. He made a loud noise. He barked and growled and showed his teeth. He pretended he was angry and hungry. He wanted to distract the hunter.

The hunter saw the fox. He forgot about Tom and Lily. He wanted to catch the fox. He followed him with his gun and his dog.

The fox was clever. He led the hunter and his dog away from the woods. He ran and dodged and hid. He made them tired and confused.

When the fox was sure they were far away, he came back to the woods. He found Tom and Lily. Tom was still lying on the ground. He was bleeding and hurt. Lily was crying and hugging him.

"Thank you, Mr. Fox, thank you for saving us!" she said.

"You're welcome, little rabbit," the fox said. "But we have to hurry. We have to get Tom to a safe place. He needs help."

The fox helped Tom to stand up. He let him lean on his back. He was gentle and careful. He led them to a nearby house. It was their house. Their mom and dad were there. They were worried and happy to see them.

They took Tom inside. They cleaned his wound and bandaged it. They gave him medicine and a hug. They thanked the fox for his help.

She saw a big tree with a lot of space for her crayons. She looked around and did not see anyone watching. She took out her red crayon and started to mark the tree. She made a big heart and wrote her name inside.

"Hey, stop that!" a voice said. Lily turned around and saw a man in a blue shirt and a hat. He had a badge and a whistle. He was a park ranger. He looked very mad. "You are breaking the law. You are hurting the tree. Give me your crayon."

Lily was scared. She did not want to give her crayon. She did not want to get in trouble. She ran to her mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench. She hugged them and cried.

The park ranger followed her and talked to her mom and dad. He told them what Lily did and why it was wrong. He said he was sorry, but he had to take her crayon. He said she could not mark the trees anymore.

Lily's mom and dad said they were sorry, too. They said they did not know Lily liked to mark the trees. They said they would teach her to respect the law and the nature. They said they would buy her a new crayon and a paper book, so she could mark as much as she wanted.

Lily felt sorry, too. She did not mean to hurt the tree or break the law. She gave her crayon to the park ranger and said she was sorry. She said she would not mark the trees anymore. She said she would mark her paper book instead.

The park ranger smiled and said he was glad. He said he hoped she would enjoy the park and have fun. He said he would give her a sticker with a tree on it, to remind her to love the trees. He said he was sorry he had to take her crayon, but he was proud of her for being honest and brave.

Lily smiled and said thank you. She took the sticker and put it on her shirt. She felt better. She hugged her mom and dad and said she loved them. She said she wanted to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. She said she was excited to mark her paper book later.

"I'm okay. But the water in the pond is getting too warm. It's making me feel sick," said Lily.

Fred thought about this and said, "I have an idea. Let's ask the powerful sun to increase the wind. That will make the water cooler."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the store with her mommy. They saw a big orange and Lily said, "Look mommy, orange!" Her mommy said, "Yes, that's an orange. Do you want to try it?" 

Lily took a bite of the orange and made a funny face. "It's bitter," she said. Her mommy explained, "Sometimes things that look good on the outside can be bitter on the inside. It's important to always try things before you decide if you like them or not." 

Lily learned that day that appearances can be deceiving and that it's important to give things a chance before making a judgement. From then on, she always tried new things and discovered many new foods that she loved.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They take turns to kick the ball and fly the kite.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He sees the ball and the kite. He wants them. He runs to Anna and Ben and says, "Give me your ball and your kite. They are mine now."

Anna and Ben are scared. They say, "No, they are not yours. They are ours. We are playing with them. Go away."

The big boy does not listen. He tries to grab the ball and the kite. Anna and Ben hold on to them. They start a fight. They pull and push and shout.

A lady sees the fight. She is a teacher. She works at the park. She blows a whistle. She says, "Stop! Stop! What are you doing? Fighting is bad. Sharing is good. Why are you fighting?"

The big boy says, "They have a ball and a kite. I want them. They are mine."

The lady says, "No, they are not yours. They are theirs. They brought them to the park. You cannot take them. That is wrong. You have to ask nicely. Maybe they will let you play with them. But you have to be nice and polite."

The big boy feels ashamed. He says, "I'm sorry. I was mean. Can I play with you?"

Anna and Ben look at each other. They are still angry. But they are also kind. They say, "Okay. You can play with us. But you have to share. And you have to be gentle. And you have to say please and thank you."

The big boy nods. He says, "Okay. I will share. And I will be gentle. And I will say please and thank you."

The lady smiles. She says, "That's good. That's how you make friends. And that's how you stay healthy. Fighting is bad for your body and your heart. Playing is good for your body and your heart. Now, let's play together. Who wants to raise the kite?"

"Look, a snake!" Sara says. She is not afraid. She likes animals.

"Let's go closer," Tom says. He is curious. He wants to touch the snake.

They walk to the snake. The snake sees them. It hisses. It is not happy. It wants to be alone.

"Hello, snake," Sara says. She smiles. She tries to pet the snake.

The snake does not like that. It wraps its tail around Sara's arm. It squeezes hard. Sara feels pain. She cries.

"Help, help!" Sara shouts. "The snake is hurting me!"

Tom is scared. He runs to get help. He sees a man with a hat. The man is a park ranger. He knows about snakes.

"Help, help!" Tom says. "My friend is in trouble! A snake is wrapping its tail around her arm!"

The park ranger follows Tom. He sees Sara and the snake. He acts fast. He grabs the snake's tail. He unwraps it from Sara's arm. He puts the snake in a bag.

"Are you okay, Sara?" the park ranger asks. He checks her arm. It is red and sore. But it is not bleeding.

"I'm okay," Sara says. She is brave. She stops crying.

"That was a mild snake," the park ranger says. "It did not bite you. But it was scared and angry. You should not touch wild animals. They can be dangerous."

"I'm sorry," Sara says. She feels sorry. She did not mean to upset the snake.

"It's okay," the park ranger says. He smiles. He is kind. "You learned a lesson. Next time, just look and admire. Do not touch."

Sara and Tom nod. They learned a lesson. They thank the park ranger. They go back to play. They do not touch any more animals. They just look and admire.

"I wanted to read the book, mom. I like books. I did not know it was heavy. I'm sorry, mom."

Anna's mom sighed. She was not angry anymore. She was glad Anna was not hurt badly. She kissed Anna's bump and said it was okay.

"I know you like books, Anna. But you have to be careful. The big book is not for you. It is for grown-ups. It has no pictures and hard words. You can read the other books on the bookshelf. They are for you. They have pictures and easy words. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded. She understood. She said sorry again.

"Can I help you clean the mess, mom?" she asked.

Anna's mom smiled. She was proud of Anna. She said yes.

"Thank you, Anna. That is very nice of you. But first, let me tie your hair. It is in your face. There, much better. Now, let's put the books back on the bookshelf. Can you hand me the books, Anna?"

Anna said yes. She handed her mom the books. They worked together and cleaned the mess. They put the big book on the top of the bookshelf. They put the other books on the lower shelves. They made the bookshelf neat and tidy.

Anna was happy. She liked to help her mom. She liked to read books. She learned a lesson. She would not climb on the chair and take the big book again. She would read the books that were for her. She hugged her mom and said she loved her.

"I love you too, Anna. You are a good girl. Now, do you want to read a book with me?"

Anna said yes. She picked a book from the bookshelf. She read it with her mom. They had fun. They laughed and learned. They enjoyed the book.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big garden with many flowers, trees and rocks. They liked to make their own landscape with sand, sticks and stones. They were proud of their work and showed it to their mom and dad.

One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Ben and he was very loud and rude. He saw Lily and Tom playing in their garden and he wanted to join them. But he did not ask nicely. He just jumped over the fence and ran to their landscape. He kicked the sand, broke the sticks and threw the stones. He laughed and said, "This is boring. Let's play something else."

Lily and Tom were very sad and angry. They had worked hard on their landscape and Ben had disturbed it. They said to him, "Go away, Ben. You are not nice. You are not our friend. You ruined our landscape. We don't want to play with you."

Ben was surprised and hurt. He did not understand why they were so mad at him. He thought he was just having fun. He said, "But I just wanted to play with you. Why are you so mean to me?"

Lily and Tom said, "You did not play with us. You played against us. You did not respect our work. You did not say sorry. You did not ask if you could join us. You were mean to us."

Ben realized that he had made a mistake. He felt sorry for what he had done. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily and Tom. I was wrong. I should have asked you first. I should have been nice to you. I should have helped you with your landscape. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends?"

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They saw that Ben was sincere. They decided to give him a chance. They said, "OK, Ben. We forgive you. We can be friends. But you have to promise to be nice to us and to our landscape. And you have to help us fix it."

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "I promise. Thank you, Lily and Tom. You are very kind. I like your landscape. It is very beautiful. Can I help you make it even better?"

Lily and Tom nodded and smiled. They said, "Yes, you can. Come on, let's work together."

They all worked together to restore their landscape. They added more sand, sticks and stones. They made it bigger and prettier. They were proud of their work and showed it to their mom and dad. They also showed it to Ben's mom and dad. They were happy and proud of their new friend.

The moral of the story is: Be respectful of other people's work and feelings. Ask before you join someone's play. Say sorry when you make a mistake. Be nice and make friends.

Lila was a girl who liked to feed the birds. She had a bag of seeds that she took to the park every day. She looked for the birds that had different colors: red, blue, yellow, green. She thought they were pretty and funny.

One day, she saw a bird that was very weak. It was lying on the grass and did not move. It had gray feathers and a black beak. Lila felt sad for the bird. She wanted to help it. She took some seeds from her bag and put them near the bird's head.

"Hello, bird," she said softly. "I have some food for you. Please eat and get better. I am your friend."

The bird opened one eye and looked at Lila. It saw the seeds and tried to peck at them. But it was too weak to lift its head. It made a weak sound, like a whisper.

"Thank you, girl," it said. "You are very kind. But I am too sick to eat. I need water and warmth. Can you help me?"

Lila nodded. She picked up the bird gently and wrapped it in her scarf. She ran to the fountain and filled her cup with water. She held the cup to the bird's beak and let it drink. She felt the bird's body get warmer and stronger.

"Thank you, girl," the bird said again. "You saved my life. You are a good friend. What is your name?"

"My name is Lila," she said. "What is your name?"

"My name is Gray," the bird said. "I am a pigeon. I got lost and hurt by a cat. I could not find my way home. Can you help me?"

Lila smiled. She knew where the pigeons lived. She had seen them on the roof of a big building. She carried Gray to the building and climbed the stairs. She found the other pigeons and put Gray down. They welcomed him and thanked Lila.

"Goodbye, Gray," she said. "I hope you feel better soon. I will come back and visit you. You are my friend."

"Goodbye, Lila," Gray said. "You are my friend too. You are the best girl in the world. I will never forget you."

Lila waved and left. She felt happy and proud. She had fed a bird and made a friend. She had done a good thing.

Sara and Tom liked to play on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shells. One day, they found a big shell that was closed. Tom said, "Maybe there is an oyster inside. Oysters are animals that live in shells. They have pearls sometimes."

Sara said, "Let's open it and see. Maybe we can find a pearl. Pearls are shiny and pretty. They are like jewels." They tried to open the shell, but it was very hard. They used a stick and a rock, but they could not open it.

Then they saw a man walking on the beach. He had a big hat and a long beard. He looked charming and friendly. He said, "Hello, children. What are you doing with that shell?"

Sara and Tom said, "We are trying to open it. We think there is an oyster inside. Maybe it has a pearl."

The man said, "That is a very big shell. It must be a very old oyster. Maybe it has a very big pearl. Do you want me to help you open it?"

Sara and Tom said, "Yes, please. Thank you, sir."

The man took the shell and used a knife to open it. He was very strong and skilled. He opened the shell and showed Sara and Tom what was inside. There was an oyster, and it had a pearl. But the pearl was not shiny and pretty. It was dull and gray. It looked like a stone.

The man said, "Oh, what a pity. This oyster has been in the shell for too long. The pearl has lost its luster. It is not worth anything."

Sara and Tom said, "Oh, no. We are sorry. We thought we would find a beautiful pearl."

The man said, "Don't be sorry. You have found something else. You have found a story. A story of a very old oyster and a very big pearl. A story that you can tell to your friends and family. A story that will increase your imagination and curiosity. A story that is more valuable than any jewel."

Sara and Tom said, "Wow. Thank you, sir. You are very kind and wise. Can we keep the shell and the pearl?"

The man said, "Of course. They are yours. Keep them as a souvenir of this day. And remember, there is beauty and wonder in everything, even in a dull and gray pearl."

She searched in his toy box, but she could not find it. Where was the teaspoon?

She tapped her brother on the shoulder and shouted. "Brother, where is the teaspoon? I need it for the cake."

Brother took off his headphones and frowned. "What teaspoon? I don't have any teaspoon. Go away, you're bothering me."

Lily was angry and sad. She wanted to make the cake, but she could not find the teaspoon. She was persistent, and she did not give up. She searched the whole house, but she could not find it. She searched the living room, but she could not find it. She searched the bathroom, but she could not find it. She searched the garage, but she could not find it. Where was the teaspoon?

She was about to cry, when she saw something shiny on the floor. She bent down and picked it up. It was the teaspoon! She was so happy, she jumped and clapped. She ran back to the kitchen, and measured the sugar. She mixed everything, and put the cake in the oven. She cleaned up the mess, and waited for the cake to bake. She was proud of herself, and she knew her mom would love the cake.

She also knew who had hidden the teaspoon. She smiled and thought of a way to get back at her brother. She had a plan, and she was persistent. She would make him eat a big slice of the cake, with a lot of salt instead of sugar. That would teach him a lesson.

Her mommy heard her and came to the living room. She saw Lily on the floor, holding her knee. She saw the open box and the chair.

Her mommy hugged her and kissed her knee. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. The box is for your birthday. It has toys and books and clothes for you. But you have to wait until tomorrow to play with them."

Her mommy smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you're curious. But sometimes you have to be patient and careful. Come on, let's put some ice on your knee and read a story together."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mommy. I love you."

"I love you too, Lily," her mommy said. They went to the couch and cuddled. Lily forgot about the box and the pain. She was happy to be with her mommy.

The moral of the story is: Listen to signs and friends. They can save your life.

"Let's go home," Mia says.

"OK," Tom says.

They walk to the gate of the park. They see a man with a flashlight. He is holding their ball.

"Hey, kids, is this your ball?" the man asks.

"Yes, it is. Thank you, mister," Tom says.

The man gives them the ball and smiles.

"Be careful, kids. It is not safe to play in the dark. You could get hurt or lost," the man says.

He explains to them why they should not play in the dark. He tells them to play in the day when they can see better.

Tom and Mia listen and nod. They understand.

"Thank you, mister. We are sorry. We will not play in the dark again," Mia says.

They say goodbye to the man and run home. They are happy to have their ball back. They decide to play soccer again tomorrow, but only in the day.

They clapped and cheered again. Then they saw a green firework. It was like a snake. They clapped and cheered some more.

"Wow, look at that one!" Tom said. He pointed to a yellow firework. It was like a smiley face. It made Tom and Lily laugh.

"That's my favorite one!" Lily said. She smiled back at the firework.

But then, something strange happened. They saw a firework that was not normal. It was not big or bright or loud. It was small and dark and quiet. It did not make a shape or a color. It just fell from the sky. It landed on the grass near them. It looked like a rock.

"What is that?" Tom asked. He was curious. He wanted to touch it.

"Don't touch it!" Lily said. She was scared. She did not like it.

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the firework. He reached out his hand. He was about to touch it.

"Tom, no!" Lily shouted. She ran after him.

But it was too late. The firework was not a rock. It was a trick. It was a bad firework. It exploded in Tom's hand. It made a loud noise. It hurt Tom's hand. It made Tom cry.

"Tom, are you okay?" Lily asked. She hugged him. She was sorry.

Their mom and dad heard the noise. They saw the firework. They saw Tom and Lily. They ran to them. They were worried.

"Tom, what happened?" their mom asked. She took his hand. She saw the burn. She was angry.

"Someone threw a bad firework. It hurt Tom's hand." Lily said. She told the truth.

"Who did that?" their dad asked. He looked around. He saw a group of boys. They were laughing. They had more bad fireworks. They were mean.

"Those boys did that. They are bad boys." Lily said. She pointed to them.

Their mom and dad saw the boys. They called the police. The police came. They took the boys away. They took the bad fireworks away. They were not allowed to play with fireworks anymore. They were in trouble.

The police also helped Tom. They gave him a bandage. They gave him a sticker. They said he was brave. They said he was lucky. They said he should never touch a firework. They said fireworks were dangerous.

Tom learned his lesson. He said he was sorry. He said he would never touch a firework again. He said he would listen to Lily. He said he would be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong bear named Ben. Ben loved to run and play outside in the woods with his animal friends. One day, Ben's friend, a little rabbit named Rosie, came to visit him.

"Hi Ben! Can we play together?" Rosie asked.

"Of course, Rosie! Let's play tag!" Ben replied.

They started to run around, but after a while, Rosie got tired and said, "I can't stay running anymore, Ben. I need to rest."

"That's okay, Rosie. You can sit and watch me run. I have a lot of power and I can run for a long time," Ben said.

Rosie watched as Ben ran around and around, amazed at his strength and fitness. After a while, Ben got tired too and said, "I need to rest now, Rosie. Let's sit and talk."

They sat down and talked about their day, and Rosie said, "I like playing with you, Ben. You are so strong and fit!"

"Thanks, Rosie. I like playing with you too. You may not have a lot of power, but you have a big heart and that's what makes you special," Ben replied.

From that day on, Ben and Rosie played together often, and they both learned that being strong and fit is important, but having a good heart is even more important.

Lila and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Sometimes they found worms, or ants, or beetles. They put them in a jar and watched them.

One day, they found something different. It was gray and hard and had many legs. It did not move or make any sound. Lila and Ben thought it was dead. They put it in the jar with the other bugs.

That night, Lila and Ben left the jar on the window sill. They went to bed and dreamed of bugs. But the gray thing was not dead. It was sleeping. And when the moon came out, it woke up. It was a firefly. It had a light in its belly that could glow.

The firefly saw the other bugs in the jar. They were scared and sad. They wanted to go out and be free. The firefly felt sorry for them. It used its light to make a hole in the lid of the jar. Then it flew out and helped the other bugs escape.

Lila and Ben woke up in the morning. They looked at the jar. It was empty. They saw a hole in the lid. They wondered what happened. They looked out the window. They saw the firefly and the other bugs flying away. They saw the firefly's light glow in the sun. They smiled and waved goodbye. They learned that some bugs are not dead, but magic.

"Where is the exit?" Lily asked.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big kite in the sky. It is red and yellow and has a long tail.

"Wow, look at the kite!" Tom says. "It is so high and fast. I want to fly a kite too."

"Me too," Lily says. "Let's go and find one."

They run to the shed. They see a small kite. It is blue and green and has a star on it. They take the kite and a string. They go to the field.

They try to fly the kite. They run and run. But the kite does not go up. It falls to the ground.

"Why does it not fly?" Tom asks. "The wind is strong. It should fly."

"Maybe the string is too short," Lily says. "Or maybe the kite is too heavy."

They look at the kite. They see a problem. The kite has a hole in it. The wind goes through the hole. The kite does not hang in the air.

"Oh no, the kite is broken," Tom says. "How can we fix it?"

"Maybe we can use a patch," Lily says. "Or some tape. Or some glue."

They look for something to fix the kite. They see a big leaf. It is brown and dry. They think it can cover the hole.

They take the leaf. They put it on the hole. They use some grass to tie it. They hope it will work.

They try to fly the kite again. They run and run. The kite goes up. It hangs in the air. It moves with the wind. It looks like a bird.

"Yay, we did it!" Tom says. "The kite is flying. It is so pretty."

"Yay, we are so smart!" Lily says. "The leaf is a good patch. It is like a wing."

They laugh and clap. They watch the kite. They are happy.

But then, something bad happens. The wind gets stronger. It blows harder. It pulls the kite. The string breaks. The kite flies away.

"Uh oh, the kite is gone," Tom says. "The wind took it. We can't get it back."

"Uh oh, that is sad," Lily says. "The kite was ours. We liked it."

They are scared. They cry. They hug each other.

They see a man. He is walking in the field. He has a hat and a coat. He sees the kite. He catches it. He brings it to them.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Is this your kite? I saw it flying in the sky. It is a nice kite. But it has a hole in it. And a leaf on it. Did you do that?"

"Yes, sir," Tom says. "The kite was broken. We tried to fix it. But the wind was too strong. It broke the string. It flew away."

"Yes, sir," Lily says. "We were scared. We thought we lost it. We were sad. Thank you for finding it."

"You're welcome, kids," he says. "You are very clever. You used a leaf to patch the hole. That is a good idea. But you need a stronger string. And a smaller hole. Do you want me to help you?"

"Yes, please," Tom and Lily say. "We want to fly the kite again. We want to have fun."

"Okay, then," he says. "Let's go to my house. I have some tools and materials. We can fix the kite together. And then we can fly it again. How does that sound?"

"Good, good," Tom and Lily say. "Thank you, thank you."

They go with the man. They fix the kite. They fly it again. They are happy. The end.

Once there was a caterpillar. It was very attractive.

He asked a bird, "Please help me fly."
The bird replied, "No, caterpillar. You cannot fly."

The caterpillar was sad. He asked other insects, like a bee and a butterfly, but they all said the same thing.

Finally the caterpillar asked a ladybug. "Please help me fly," he requested.
The ladybug smiled. "I can help you, caterpillar. It involves something called 'metamorphosis'."
The caterpillar was so excited. He thanked the ladybug.

The caterpillar began his journey to his beautiful butterfly form. He fulfilled his request and was now able to fly.
The caterpillar was so happy. He spread his wings and flew around the garden, feeling free and attractive.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. He opened his eyes and saw a small rabbit. The rabbit said, "Come play with me in the forest! It's so much fun!" The goat hopped up and followed the rabbit.

The two friends explored the forest, chased butterflies, and played hide-and-seek. After a few hours, the rabbit said it was time to take a nap. The goat nodded, yawned, and lay down in the grass. As he fell asleep, he felt happy, content, and so very smart.

But before the rat could do anything, Joe heard a voice from behind him. It was an old man, coming out of a nearby bush. He said "Don't be afraid my friend, I won't let this rat hurt you." The old man leaned down and grabbed the rat by its tail, lifting it high in the air. The rat squirmed and tried to break free, but the man held tight.

The old man said, "I think we can both go our separate ways now, right?" Joe was so relieved. He quickly said goodbye to the old man and ran away, never to stumble again.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Teddy. Teddy lived in a big, cold cave with lots of ice. One day, he decided to escape.

Teddy looked around and suddenly he saw something. It was a jar of pepper! Teddy knew he liked pepper, so he grabbed it quickly and started running. He ran and ran and ran until the cave was out of sight.

Teddy was so happy - he had escaped! But he was still very cold. Then he had an idea - he sprinkled the pepper over himself! It kept him warm and cozy in the icy forest.

Teddy smiled. He was sure glad he had escaped the cave!

The little bird didn't like the harsh taste of pepper, but the rabbit didn't believe him. So the little bird decided to sing a song about how much he disliked pepper. The rabbit listened to the song and realized that everyone has different tastes. From that day on, the rabbit stopped eating so much pepper and tried new foods instead. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to respect other people's preferences and try new things. The little bird's song about pepper was a setup for the payoff of the rabbit learning a valuable lesson. And of course, the little bird continued to sing his beautiful songs every morning.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She woke up early today because she was very busy. She had to go to school and then to the park with her mommy.

Lily's mommy asked her, "Do you want to pray before we leave?" Lily nodded her head and they both prayed together.

At school, Lily's friend Tommy took her favorite toy and wouldn't give it back. Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. She told her teacher and her teacher helped her talk to Tommy. Tommy said sorry and gave the toy back to Lily.

After school, Lily and her mommy went to the park. They saw a bird with a hurt wing. Lily's mommy said, "Let's pray for the bird to feel better." They prayed and the bird flew away. Lily felt happy that they helped the bird.

One day, Lily's friend came over to play. But her friend was rude and didn't like the lamp. She said it was ugly and old. Lily felt sad but didn't say anything.

Later that day, Lily's friend accidentally knocked over the lamp and it broke into tiny pieces. Lily was so upset and cried a lot. She knew the lamp belonged to her grandma and she couldn't fix it. 

Lily's friend said sorry, but it was too late. Lily's grandma came over and saw the broken lamp. She was very sad and disappointed. Lily felt terrible that she didn't stand up for her lamp and let her rude friend break it. From then on, Lily learned to speak up for what she loved and to not let anyone be rude to her things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a thick blanket that she loved to snuggle with at night. One day, Lily's mommy noticed a hole in the blanket and decided to sew it up with a needle and thread. 

Lily was curious and wanted to peek at what her mommy was doing. She snuck up behind her mommy and accidentally bumped into her. The needle poked Lily's finger and it hurt a lot. 

Lily cried and cried, but her mommy kissed her finger and made it all better. However, a few days later, Lily's finger started to hurt again. Her mommy took her to the doctor and they found out that the needle had left a tiny piece inside her finger. They had to do a surgery to remove it, and Lily was very scared. 

After the surgery, Lily's finger got infected and she had to stay in the hospital for a long time. She missed her blanket and her mommy so much. When she finally got better and went home, she found out that her blanket had been thrown away. Lily was very sad and missed her blanket every night. The end.

As she walked home, Lily saw a big, scary dog. She was afraid it might chase her, but then she remembered her whistle. She blew it as loud as she could, and the dog ran away.

Later that day, Lily went to the store with her mom. She saw a toy that she really wanted, but she didn't have enough money. Suddenly, she remembered the penny in her pocket. She used it to buy the toy, and it made her so happy.

From then on, Lily always kept her penny and whistle with her. She knew they were special and could help her whenever she needed them.
